title: Install.performInstall hardcodes forceConflicts: false on the Create path, ignoring Install.ForceConflicts
body: ### What happened?  `Install.performInstall` passes `forceConflicts: false` to `KubeClient.Create` when creating resources during a fresh install (no resources to adopt). The `Install.ForceConflicts` field is ignored on this path.  https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/pkg/action/install.go#L518-L521  ```go if len(toBeAdopted) == 0 && len(resources) > 0 {     _, err = i.cfg.KubeClient.Create(         resources,         kube.ClientCreateOptionServerSideApply(i.ServerSideApply, false)) // <-- hardcoded false ```  `ForceConflicts` is only passed through on the `Update` path (line 528), which is used when there are existing resources to adopt:  ```go kube.ClientUpdateOptionServerSideApply(i.ServerSideApply, i.ForceConflicts), ```  This means that if a resource in the chart already exists with a different field manager (e.g. from a previous failed install that was rolled back but left the resource behind), the SSA create fails with a 409 conflict that cannot be forced through — even when `ForceConflicts` is set to `true`.  ### How to reproduce  1. Install a chart that includes both a Custom Resource and a controller that SSA-applies to that same CR on startup 2. Cause the install to fail after the CR and controller are created (e.g. timeout) 3. Uninstall the failed release 4. The CR may survive the uninstall with a field manager entry from the controller 5. Retry the install with `--force-conflicts` — `KubeClient.Create` is called with `forceConflicts: false`, hits the conflict, and fails 6. Every subsequent retry fails identically  ### What did you expect to happen?  `forceConflicts` should be passed through on the `Create` path, same as the `Update` path:  ```go if len(toBeAdopted) == 0 && len(resources) > 0 {     _, err = i.cfg.KubeClient.Create(         resources,         kube.ClientCreateOptionServerSideApply(i.ServerSideApply, i.ForceConflicts)) ```  ### Helm version  Affects `main` branch and all v4.x releases.  ### Kubernetes version  ``` Server Version: v1.35.2

title: Transitive dependency resolution
body: ### What would you like to be added?  In complex helm charts, some charts added as dependencies can depend on the same chart at different (compatible or incompatible) versions.  For example:  ```yaml name: chart-A:   dependencies:   - name: chart-B     version: 1.0.0   - name: chart-C     version: 1.0.0   - name: chart-D     version: 1.0.0 ``` ```yaml name: chart-B:   dependencies:   - name: chart-D     version: 1.1.0 ``` ```yaml name: chart-C:   dependencies:   - name: chart-D     version: 2.0.0 ``` In this case, both `chart-A` and `chart-B` can be built with `chart-D-1.1.0`. Instead `chart-C` needs the templates defined by `chart-D` in version `2.0.0` and cannot use version `1.1.0` because it's incompatible.  For those cases, helm should provide a resolution strategy and it should be clearly documented.  Since helm chart versions must be valid in semver, helm could support all of the following: - Select all the needed versions (in the example `chart-D-1.1.0` and `chart-D-2.0.0`) - raising an error when incompatible versions are requested - provide all the incompatible versions with the right scope (in the example above, `chart-D-1.1.0` for `chart-A` and `chart-B` and `chart-D-2.0.0` for building `chart-C`)  ### Why is this needed?  To support complex helm chart scenarios in which the same dependency (e.g. a [common library](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/library_charts/#the-common-helm-helper-chart)) is transitively required in multiple versions without creating a [dependency hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_hell)

title: Remove YAML separator whitespace-trim workaround in Chart v3
body: ### What would you like to be added?  For Charts **apiVersion v3**, remove the special-case normalization logic that handles Go template whitespace trimming (`{{-`) gluing content to YAML document separators (`---`).  Given a template like:  ```yaml --- {{- include "mychart.service" . }} ```  the `{{-` trims the newline after `---`, producing this raw rendered output:  ``` ---apiVersion: v1 kind: Service ... ```  Helm currently has special handling to detect and correct this before passing manifests to YAML parsers or post-renderers. In v3, Helm should no longer compensate for this — chart authors should write:  ```yaml --- {{ include "mychart.service" . }} ```  or omit the explicit `---` entirely (Helm adds document separators automatically).  Per the Go [`text/template`](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template#hdr-Text_and_spaces) spec, `{{-` trims all leading whitespace (space, tab, carriage return, newline) from the following text — this is standard, well-documented behavior.  A migration note should be added to the **Charts v2 → v3 migration guide** documenting this change.  ### Why is this needed?  The special-case logic adds complexity to Helm's template rendering pipeline (introduced as part of the fix in #31868). Charts apiVersion v3 is the right opportunity to remove it.  Dropping this workaround also aligns Helm's behaviour with standard Go template semantics. Chart authors familiar with Go templates expect `{{-` to only trim leading whitespace. The current special handling means Helm silently produces different output than what Go templates specify, which is surprising and hard to reason about. By removing it in v3, chart authors can apply their Go template knowledge directly, without needing workarounds or being caught off guard by Helm-specific behaviour.  **Compatibility constraints:**  - **apiVersion v1/v2 charts (Helm 3 and Helm 4)**: The special handling **must be preserved** indefinitely. A large number of charts in the wild use `{{-` after `---` separat

title: bug: prepareUpgrade returns wrong error variable when release conversion fails
body: ### What happened?  In `pkg/action/upgrade.go`, the `prepareUpgrade` function returns the wrong error variable on line 256. When `Deployed()` succeeds (`err == nil`) but `releaserToV1Release()` fails (`cerr != nil`), the function returns `err` (nil) instead of `cerr`, causing the caller to receive a nil error with nil release data.  ```go currentReleasei, err := u.cfg.Releases.Deployed(name) var cerr error currentRelease, cerr = releaserToV1Release(currentReleasei) if cerr != nil {     return nil, nil, false, err  // BUG: should be cerr } ```  This means a successful `Deployed()` call paired with a failed conversion silently returns `(nil, nil, false, nil)` — appearing as success with no data, which can lead to nil pointer dereferences downstream.  ### What did you expect to happen?  The conversion error (`cerr`) should be returned so the caller knows the operation failed, rather than silently returning nil.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  While reviewing the upgrade error handling path, I noticed that `prepareUpgrade` returns the wrong error variable when the release conversion fails.  The issue occurs when: 1. The last release is in a non-deployed status (e.g. `StatusFailed` or `StatusSuperseded`) 2. `Deployed()` succeeds and returns a valid releaser (`err == nil`) 3. `releaserToV1Release()` fails to convert it (`cerr != nil`) 4. Line 256 returns `err` (nil from step 2) instead of `cerr` (the actual failure)  The result is `(nil, nil, false, nil)` — the caller sees no error but has no release data, risking a nil pointer dereference on subsequent access to `currentRelease`.  Today, all storage drivers return v1 releases so the conversion always succeeds, but the error handling is incorrect and would surface as a silent failure if the storage layer evolves (e.g. a new release format in Helm v4).  ### Helm version  <details>  ```console $ helm version Applies to main branch (v4-dev) at commit 1be395e7 ``` </details>  ### Kubern

title: No way to figure out where Helm chart came from
body: ### What would you like to be added?  This is insane: once a Helm chart is installed, there is literally no reasonable way to figure out where the manifests originated from.  Helm stores release data as encoded secrets. These blobs contain rendered manifests, chart content, and values. But they do not, and cannot, reliably tell you what OCI repository or registry the chart was pulled from. The feeds by design live on the user machine and not in the cluster (?!)  Even if you decode every layer of the secret, there’s no structured source information. You cannot audit, trace, or verify the origin from the cluster itself. You are completely dependent on external logs or human memory.  Meanwhile, Kubernetes supports exactly what you need via CRDs: a structured, queryable resource could have recorded chart mutations and source provenance. Helm ignores this and instead pollutes secrets with opaque binary blobs.  The result: Helm remembers what was installed, but actively forgets where it came from, making supply chain verification and auditing basically impossible.  This isn’t a minor inconvenience — it’s a fundamental blind spot for anyone using Helm in production.  ### Why is this needed?  Status quo is absolutely insane

Flux's post-renderer is a Kustomize build, and Kustomize does not allow multiple objects with the same fully-qualified name.  The solution is processing hooks separately from resource templates (i.e. passing them to post-renderers separately), so hooks and templates can continue to overlap as it was supported in Helm 3.

title: YAML block scalars containing long dash sequences regression
body: ### What happened?  A zarf user reported an [issue](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf/issues/4754) with the recent update to helm `v4.1.3` whereby a helm chart could no longer be templated. They were able to isolate the issue to a resource containing:  ```yaml apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: Job metadata:   name: hook-job spec:   template:     spec:       restartPolicy: Never       containers:         - name: c           image: example.com/repro:1.0           command:             - /bin/sh             - -c             - |               echo -------------------               resp=$(curl -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code}\n" -k -X POST --url http://localhost:8080/api/metadata/workflow -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "@"$file)               echo ------------------- ```  `fixDocSeparators` (introduced in #31868) scans rendered templates for `---` to fix missing newlines after document separators caused by Go template whitespace trimming ({{-).  The scanning loop has a bug: when it finds `---` mid-line (not a separator) it correctly rejects it, but only advances 3 characters. If the rejected `---` was part of a longer dash sequence (e.g. `echo --------------------` in a block scalar), the next iteration sees `---` at position 0 of the remaining buffer and misidentifies it as a line-start separator, inserting newlines.  This turns: ``` - |    echo -------------------- ``` into: ``` - | echo ------ --- --- --- --- -- ``` Those injected --- lines are then parsed as YAML document separators by kio.ParseAll in annotateAndMerge, producing a MalformedYAMLError.   ### What did you expect to happen?  No change in behavior from previous versions of helm.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  This only affects charts using a post-renderer (which triggers the `annotateAndMerge` path) - helm template alone is unaffected. title: Subchart default nil values shadow global values via pluck (regression from #31644)
body: ## What happened?  After the fix for #31643 (PR #31644, backported to 3.20.x via #31829), nil values declared in a subchart's `values.yaml` are now preserved in the merged values map during coalescing. When a template uses Sprig's `pluck` to implement a local-then-global-then-default fallback pattern, these nil values are returned as the first match, shadowing the global value.  This is a regression introduced in 3.20.1 by the backport of #31644 (PR #31829). Helm 3.20.0 is not affected. Helm 4.1.1 is also not affected.  The root cause is in `coalesceTablesFullKey` in `pkg/chartutil/coalesce.go`. The `srcOriginalNonNil` guard added by #31644 (backported to v3 via #31829) correctly prevents deletion of user-specified nils, but it also prevents cleanup of nil values that come from **chart defaults** during subsequent coalesce passes.  Before #31644, the unconditional `delete(dst, key)` at `ok && !merge && dv == nil` would clean up these nils. With the new `srcOriginalNonNil[key]` guard, nils from chart defaults survive into the final values map.  Note: Helm v4 has the same `coalesceTablesFullKey` code but is not affected — it likely handles this through a different code path elsewhere in the v4 chart processing pipeline.  See also: [gitlab-org/charts/gitlab#6366](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/charts/gitlab/-/work_items/6366) — the downstream GitLab chart issue reporting this behavior.  ## What did you expect to happen?  Nil values from subchart chart defaults (not explicitly set by the user) should not appear in the final merged values. They should either be stripped or not copied in the first place, so that `pluck` falls through to the global value.  ## How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  No custom chart needed — this reproduces with the published [GitLab Helm chart](https://charts.gitlab.io/), which uses a `pluck`-based fallback pattern in its templates.  ### Setup  ```bash helm repo add gitlab https://charts.gitlab.io/ helm repo update

title: performance: Add optional JSON database backend to reduce deserialization overhead on full release queries
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Add support for an optional JSON document database driver for Helm release storage.  The new driver would: 1. Store release metadata in a queryable JSON format (e.g., MongoDB, Couchbase, or embedded JSON store) 2. Support indexed queries on common fields (name, namespace, chart, status, timestamps) 3. Allow partial retrieval without full deserialization of all releases 4. Be opt-in via a flag like `--driver=jsondb` to maintain backward compatibility  This is an initial discussion to gauge interest before potentially writing a formal HIP.  ### Why is this needed?  ## Performance Problem  When managing a large number of releases (1000+), full listing operations become increasingly slow: - `helm list` (especially with `--all` or across namespaces) - `helm status` (when scanning for specific release) - Release history queries  Profiling shows most time is spent on **deserialization** of release data from the stored format.  ## Use Case  Large platforms / multi-tenant clusters where: - Hundreds of releases are managed per namespace - Frequent listing/filtering operations are required - CI/CD pipelines need fast release status checks  ## Expected Benefit  - **Faster queries**: Indexed lookups instead of full scan + deserialize - **Better scalability**: Performance degrades gracefully with release count - **Flexibility**: Users can choose backend based on their infrastructure  ## Environment - Storage driver: [Secret/ConfigMap/SQL] - Approximate release count: 1500+

title: Decouple pkg/cli from pkg/kube to avoid import cycles for library consumers
body: ### What would you like to be added?  I'm doing the prep work for https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/issues/4401 which aims to import Helm as a Go library in kustomize instead of using the helm binary. I found that any package that depends on `pkg/cli` creates an import cycle. I realized this is because [pkg/cli/environment.go](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/pkg/cli/environment.go) imports `pkg/kube`, which pulls in `fluxcd/cli-utils`, then `k8s.io/cli-runtime`, then `sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api` creating a cycle back to our own module.  I'd suggest decoupling `pkg/cli.EnvSettings` from `pkg/kube`. Currently `environment.go` imports `pkg/kube` (for the `RESTClientGetter` in `Namespace()` and `GetConfig()`), which makes it impossible for kustomize to use any Helm package that depends on `pkg/cli`, since `cli-runtime` already imports `kustomize/api`.  If possible, maybe split `EnvSettings` into a pure-config struct (paths, namespace, debug flags, no kube imports) in a separate lightweight package, and keep the Kubernetes client setup in `pkg/cli` or `pkg/kube`. I also found the [TODO: refactor this out of pkg/action](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/v4.1.3/pkg/action/pull.go#L39) comment on `Pull.Settings` which kinda suggests this direction was already considered? Not sure.   ### Why is this needed?  PR #13617 enabled using Helm as a Go library. But kustomize sits on both sides of the `cli-runtime` dependency graph, it's imported BY `cli-runtime` and now it wants to import Helm. This creates an import cycle for any Helm package that touches `pkg/cli`.  Currently this limits kustomize to `pkg/engine`, `pkg/chart/*`, and `pkg/registry`. The `pkg/action`, `pkg/downloader`, `pkg/getter`, and `pkg/repo` packages are all unreachable due to the cycle through `pkg/cli` -> `pkg/kube` -> `cli-runtime` -> `kustomize/api`.

title: Registry Login with HTTPS URL
body: ## Context  Since Helm v4.1.0 it is not possible anymore to login into a registry using a URL with `http://` or `https://`, due to the changes from #31519. For example, the following command:  ```bash gcloud auth application-default print-access-token | helm registry login -u oauth2accesstoken --password-stdin https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev ```  will now produce the following error:  ``` level=WARN msg="registry login currently only supports registry hostname, not a repository path" host=https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev suggested=https: Error: invalid reference: invalid registry "https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev" ```  ## Discussion / Question  I would like to open the discussion on if this is intended behavior or an unintended side-effect of the change. Some places like Google or JFrog use HTTPS URLs in their documentation when authenticating using `helm login` ([Google's documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/helm/authentication#token) & [JFrog's documentation](https://docs.jfrog.com/artifactory/docs/kubernetes-helm-chart-repositories#connect-your-helm-oci-client-to-artifactory)). On the other hand, other platforms like Azure don't include the `http/s` prefix in their documentation.  The question is now, which is actually "correct"? Should it be allowed to login using an `http/s` URL or should users be forced to drop the protocol? This could however cause some existing workflows to break.  What do you guys think?

title: Regression from Helm 3: annotateAndMerge corrupts manifests when rendered template content has --- followed by no newline
body: Hi team!  When a chart template has `---` followed by `{{- include ... }}` (note the `{{-` which trims whitespace), the Go template `{{-` directive trims the newline after `---`, producing `---apiVersion: v1\n...` as the raw rendered content. This can happen at the start of a template file or between documents in a multi-document template.  In Helm v4, the new `annotateAndMerge()` function in `pkg/action/action.go` parses this content with `kio.ParseAll()` before sending it to post-renderers. `kio.ParseAll()` correctly (per the YAML spec) interprets `---apiVersion` as a YAML mapping key — not a document separator followed by a mapping — and then re-serializes it as `'---apiVersion': v1`. This corrupts the manifest — the resource loses its `apiVersion` field entirely.  The bug only triggers when a `PostRenderer` is set (since `annotateAndMerge` is only called in the `if pr != nil` branch). The Helm CLI doesn't use a post-renderer by default, which is why `helm install` and `helm template` work fine. However, the Helm SDK is used by projects like [Flux helm-controller](https://github.com/fluxcd/helm-controller), which always sets a PostRenderer to inject origin labels — causing all such charts to fail.  Related issue: https://github.com/fluxcd/helm-controller/issues/1423  ### Regression  This is a regression from Helm v3. In v3, the post-renderer received the raw manifest bytes directly — no YAML round-trip:  ```go // Helm v3 - pkg/action/action.go if pr != nil {     b, err = pr.Run(b) } ```  In v4, commit e6362d74c ("Allow post-renderer to process hooks") introduced `annotateAndMerge()`, which parses all rendered templates through `kio.ParseAll()` and re-serializes them to inject `postrenderer.helm.sh/postrender-filename` annotations before passing to the post-renderer. This YAML round-trip is what corrupts the manifest.  Note: `kio.ParseAll()` is correct per the YAML spec — `---` is only a document separator when it's on its own line. title: Feature Request: Support polling for kstatus
body: Hi team 👋   As discussed in the Helm dev meeting, I'm opening this issue to track the implementation of the `poller` wait strategy, an addition to Helm's kstatus implementation (pairing with the current/default `watcher`).  As pointed out in the dev meeting by @joejulian (who wants to use the `watcher` strategy in Flux), giving users the flexbility to choose between watching and polling is extremely relevant: some may choose to put the onus on the Kubernetes API Server via polling, some may choose to put the onus on the process running the Helm SDK (e.g. a controller) via watchers.  As part of introducing this new wait strategy, I propose also splitting the `WatchUntilReady` API into two (of course, in a non-breaking way):  * `WaitForHooks` * `WaitForTests`  Currently, Helm tests share a lof of code with hooks. This split allows for early cancellation of tests only, which is a behavior we want to introduce in Flux: users probably want to bail out fast from Helm tests if a new config arrives, but not bail out fast from Helm hooks, which are potentially running production database migrations.  Another benefit of this split is renaming `WatchUntilReady` to what it actually means in the Helm codebase: waiting on hooks/tests.  To make this change non-breaking we can use Helm's well-established pattern of mini-interfaces: if the `kube.Waiter` returned by `kube.Interface.GetWaiter` (or now `kube.Interface.GetWaiterWithOptions`) implements the two new methods we use them, otherwise we use `WatchUntilReady`.  Please assign this issue to me 🙏

title: isMatchingInfo compares full GVK causing resource deletion when API version changes
body: ### What happened?  When upgrading a Helm release where a custom resource changes API version (e.g., from `v2beta1` to `v2beta2` of the same CRD), Helm 4 incorrectly treats the old and new versions as **different resources**. This causes it to **delete the old version** (which is the same underlying object in etcd) after creating the new version, effectively deleting the resource that was just created.  The wait then times out because the resource no longer exists:  ``` timeout waiting for: [CrdUpgradeTestb/default/b status: 'NotFound'] ```  ### Root Cause  In https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/12581, `isMatchingInfo` in `pkg/kube/resource.go` was changed from comparing **Kind + Group** (ignoring Version) to comparing the **full `GroupVersionKind` struct** (including Version):  ```go // Before (Helm 3.x): func isMatchingInfo(a, b *resource.Info) bool {     return a.Name == b.Name && a.Namespace == b.Namespace &&         a.Mapping.GroupVersionKind.Kind == b.Mapping.GroupVersionKind.Kind &&         a.Mapping.GroupVersionKind.Group == b.Mapping.GroupVersionKind.Group }  // After (Helm 4): func isMatchingInfo(a, b *resource.Info) bool {     return a.Name == b.Name && a.Namespace == b.Namespace &&         a.Mapping.GroupVersionKind == b.Mapping.GroupVersionKind } ```  This means that when a resource changes API version (e.g., `crd-upgrades.example.com/v2beta1` → `crd-upgrades.example.com/v2beta2`), `Difference()` considers them as non-matching. Helm's `update()` method then:  1. **Creates/updates** the new version (`v2beta2`) of the resource 2. Computes `originals.Difference(targets)` — the old version (`v2beta1`) is in the difference set because it doesn't match the new version 3. **Deletes** the old version — but since both versions share the same underlying storage in the Kubernetes API server, this deletes the resource that was just created in step 1 4. title: `helm uninstall --wait` with kstatus watcher times out on resources deletion
body: ### Helm version  ``` 4.1.0 ```  ### Kubernetes version  ``` K3s v1.31.x (also reproducible on other distributions) ```  ### Describe the bug  After upgrading to Helm 4.1.0, our integration tests running on GitHub Actions workflows started failing intermittently during `helm uninstall`.  When using `helm uninstall --wait --cascade foreground`, the new kstatus-based StatusWatcher (default in Helm 4.1.0) intermittently reports `actualStatus=Terminating` indefinitely for resources (ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Services and ServiceAccounts), even after Kubernetes has successfully deleted them.  **This is a flaky issue** - it does not occur on every uninstall, but happens frequently enough to cause CI failures. The issue appears to be a race condition in how the kstatus watcher tracks deletion status of resources during foreground cascade deletion. This issue did not occur with Helm 4.0.x.  When it occurs, the Kubernetes garbage collector removes the `foregroundDeletion` finalizer and deletes the resources within milliseconds, but Helm's status watcher never detects the deletion and waits until the timeout expires.  Using `--wait=legacy` works correctly and does not exhibit this flaky behavior.  This might be related to https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/31421 which introduced the new `--wait` flag strategies in Helm 4.1.0.  ### To Reproduce  1. title: Support for side-by-side installs of Helm v3 and v4 with Chocolatey on Windows
body: ### What would you like to be added?  With the chocolatey [kubernetes-helm](https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/kubernetes-helm) package ([ref](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/#from-chocolatey-windows)), there is currently no easy way to install v3 and v4 side-by-side on Windows. This is due to the [Chocolatey standards](https://docs.chocolatey.org/en-us/create/create-packages/#naming-packages-to-allow-for-side-by-side-installation) for supporting side-by-side where the expectation is to "Create separate package IDs for each major version".  So for example, there could be `kubernetes-helm3` and `kubernetes-helm4` packages, and then the `kubernetes-helm` package could be a [metapackage](https://docs.chocolatey.org/en-us/getting-started/#terminology) that depends on the `kubernetes-helm4` package.  ### Why is this needed?  Support for side-by-side installs of Helm v3 and v4 with Chocolatey on Windows would be useful for managing the Helm version installed in our CI/CD environments where our users use the `helm` CLI during their builds / deployments. Our users currently use v3 but would like the option to update to v4 or to pin to v3, so we would need both versions installed.

title: Feature Request: Add Flag to Override/Replace Auto-Appended Chart Name When Pushing to OCI
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Hi Helm team,  I’d like to request a feature enhancement related to pushing charts to OCI registries (such as AWS ECR).  Currently, in Helm v3.17, Helm automatically appends the chart name from Chart.yaml when pushing to an OCI registry.  **Example:**  ```Chart.yaml``` ``` name: app version: 1.0.0 ```  **Command:**  ```helm push app-1.0.0.tgz oci://ecr.io/test/app-charts```   **Result:**  ```ecr.io/test/app-charts/app:1.0.0```   Helm automatically adds /app based on the chart name.  ### Previous Behavior  In Helm v3.6.0, I was able to push directly to:  ```ecr.io/test/app-charts:1.0.0```   without Helm modifying the repository path.  This allowed more flexibility in defining repository naming conventions.  ### Feature Request  Please consider adding a flag to allow users to **replace or override the auto-generated** repository name.  **Example (proposed):** ``` helm push app-1.0.0.tgz oci://ecr.io/test/app-charts \   --override-name app-charts ```  or ``` helm push app-1.0.0.tgz oci://ecr.io/test/app-charts \   --no-auto-name ```  or ``` helm push app-1.0.0.tgz oci://ecr.io/test/app-charts \   --target-repo app-charts ```  Any similar option that allows full control over the final OCI path would be very helpful.  ### Why is this needed?  ### Current Limitation  The automatic chart name appending cannot be overridden.  This makes it difficult to: - Follow predefined repository structures - Use shared repositories - Maintain backward compatibility with existing registries

title: Avoid using and setting a global slog
body: ### What would you like to be added?  As a Helm SDK I would like Helm to avoid using `slog.Info/Debug/Warn` and statements and instead use a logger I can pass in.  As a user who embeds the entire Helm CLI into my project I would like Helm to avoid relying on setting a global default logger. https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/40a9de1086bfd97f5e7a456c60221324b95e72f1/pkg/cmd/root.go#L133 Of course, I can send in my own logger, but then it will change the Helm UX, and will make flags like `--color` irrelevant  ### Why is this needed?  From an SDK perspective, unless I'm setting my global logger before certain function calls, I will miss out on pertinent logs. See https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/31717.   As a user embedding Helm, it's inconvenient to have to set a global slogger.  Ideally I could pass in a logger at the CLI level and it would be propagated throughout the codebase. This would also allow SDK users to send in a logger when they need to.

title: Flogging a dead horse - providing access to a real global context
body: ### What would you like to be added?  I understand that I'm kind of flogging a dead horse, but still—**the global context is really needed**.  If we analyze the history of various submitted issues like [this](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/11232), or [this](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12115), or [this](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/7915), it will become clear that people often need to access the **_real_** global context from within various parts of the templates. And existing solutions, IMVHO, are not good enough.  Please, read below.    ### Why is this needed?  Well, let's look at this template:  ``` {{- define "master.backend.name" -}} {{- default $.Chart.Name .name | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }} {{- end }} ```  What we have here is the `define` directive. And if this directive is later included via an `include` function, then the author that wrote the directive must think about the possible contexts provided by the `include`, or vise-versa, the writer of the include must know the internals of the define in order to understand what context the `define` actually expects.  **This fundamentally breaks the separation of concepts**. Like, in programming languages, the functions provide an interface, a given API to the caller in the form of a particular contract. The function is never ever making an assumption of who is going to call it. It is not the function's job to think about that.   Of course we may say that `directive` is never supposed to act like a function in the sense like above etc. But this is not about function. It is about encapsulation. When writing the `include`, **I have to look at the definition of the `define` directive, I have to know the internal implementation (!). Otherwise I might make a mistake, and it may not render at all or worse—render incorrectly.** It is like an _"implicit contract"_. title: Add a way to change default {{ and }} template delimiters
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Add an ability to set `Delims` (https://pkg.go.dev/text/template#Template.Delims) in go templates.  I think it could be done using cli-flags or something like that.  All we need is add `Delims` function after all `New` functions (like here: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/cb78d7f7f3126b392d073a5a7e0cbb1e39c52d73/pkg/engine/engine.go#L289)  It could be something like that but without hardcoded values ```golang t.New(filename).Delims("[%", "%]").Parse(r.tpl) ```   ### Why is this needed?  When we have several layers of templating (something like jinja2+helm) it is required to use some ugly approaches to escape helm templating while files are templating by another engine first.  I know that `jinja2` can change its own delimiters but it is just an example - it could be another engine which also uses `{{` and `}}` but without ability to change them.   Another example with `PrometheusRule`.  We have to do something like that: ```yaml         - alert: GitlabRunnerMissingExportMount           expr: gitlab_runner_missing_export           for: 5m           labels:             gitlabrunner: count           annotations:             summary: |-               GitLab Runner missing /export mountpoint             description: |-               GitLab Runner '{{ printf "{{ $labels.gitlab_runner_name }}" }}' does not have '/export' filesystem mounted. ```  With custom delimiters it could be just: ```yaml         - alert: GitlabRunnerMissingExportMount           expr: gitlab_runner_missing_export           for: 5m           labels:             gitlabrunner: count           annotations:             summary: |-               GitLab Runner missing /export mountpoint             description: |-               GitLab Runner '{{ $labels.gitlab_runner_name }}' does not have '/export' filesystem mounted. ```  And the whole value would be passed to manifest to allow prometheus use it as is.

title: tag AND condition logic in subcharts
body: Currently, Helm evaluates subchart dependencies using `condition OR tag`.    Example:  Chart.yaml: ```yaml dependencies:   - name: item-a     condition: item-a.enabled     tags:       - group-a    - name: item-b     condition: item-b.enabled     tags:       - group-a    ```  values.yaml: ```yaml tags:   group-a: false item-a:   enabled: true ``` Observed behavior:  Even though the tag **group-a** is set to false, **item-a** is still installed because the enabled condition is true.  This makes it impossible to fully disable a group of charts using tags alone.    Expected behavior:   - If `tags.group-a` is false, all charts under that tag should not install, even if `enabled=true`.    Desired behavior table:  | tag  | enabled | Installed? | |------|---------|------------| | false | true   | ❌ No     | | true  | false  | ❌ No     | | true  | true   | ✅ Yes    | | false | false  | ❌ No     |

When `helm pull` encounters an OCI Image Index (`application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`): 1. Iterate through manifests in the index 2. Find the manifest with `artifactType: application/vnd.cncf.helm.config.v1+json` (or matching `config.mediaType`) 3. Pull that specific manifest  Example OCI Image Index containing both container image and Helm chart:  ```json {   "schemaVersion": 2,   "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json",   "manifests": [     {       "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",       "digest": "sha256:abc...",       "platform": { "architecture": "amd64", "os": "linux" }     },     {       "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",       "digest": "sha256:def...",       "artifactType": "application/vnd.cncf.helm.config.v1+json"     }   ] } ```  ## Why is this needed?  Currently, `helm pull` fails when an OCI repository tag points to an Image Index:  ``` Error: unable to retrieve blob with digest sha256:xxx: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json: not found ```  Container runtimes (Docker, Podman) already handle Image Index by selecting manifests via `platform` field. Helm could use the same pattern with `artifactType`.  **Benefits:** - Single source of truth: one tag for both the application image and its deployment chart - Simplified CI/CD: publish once, consume differently based on tool - Consistent versioning between image and chart - Aligns with OCI 1.1 artifact model  **Current workarounds:** - Use separate tags (`:0.0.5` for image, `:chart-0.0.5` for chart) - Use separate repository paths (`/app` for image, `/app/chart` for chart)  **Related:** - OCI Image Spec 1.1 Image Index: https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/image-index.md - OCI Distribution Spec 1.1 artifactType: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md - Previous

title: Helm 4 integrate lint exlusion list
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Hello, my name is Danilo Patrucco,   I am proposing an enhancement to the helm lint command to include an exclusion capability. This feature would involve the introduction of a .helmlintignore file, which would list files and specific errors found within those files. If an error occurs during linting and it matches a pattern specified in the .helmlintignore file, that error will not be displayed.  Additionally, we plan to introduce a --lint-ignore-file flag. title: Helm Template Context Bug: Nested Helper Functions Lose Root Context Access
body: ### What happened?  When a Helm helper template is called with a string parameter, nested helper calls within that template lose access to the root context (`.Values`, `.Chart`, etc.), even when explicitly passing `.` or `$.` to the nested helper.    ## Expected Behavior Nested helper functions should maintain access to the root Helm context when the parent helper explicitly passes `.` or `$.` as the context parameter.  ## Actual Behavior Nested helper functions receive the string parameter passed to the parent helper instead of the root context, causing errors when trying to access `.Values` fields.    ## Error Message ``` Error: template: myapp/templates/_helpers.tpl:X:Y: executing "myapp.childHelper"  at <.Values.features.enabled>: can't evaluate field Values in type string ```   ## Root Cause Analysis  1. **Call Chain**:    - Template calls: `{{- include "myapp.parentHelper" "my-template-name" }}`    - Parent helper receives: `.` = `"my-template-name"` (string)    - Parent helper calls: `{{- include "myapp.childHelper" . }}`    - Child helper receives: `.` = `"my-template-name"` (string)  2. **Context Loss**:    - The string `"my-template-name"` becomes the context (`.`) for the parent helper    - When parent helper calls child with `.`, it passes the string, not root context    - Child helper tries `{{.Values.features.enabled}}` on string → **ERROR**  3. **Failed Workarounds**:    - Using `$.Values` instead of `.Values` → Same error    - Both `.` and `$` resolve to the string parameter in nested context   ## Impact This behavior limits the ability to create reusable, composable helper templates and forces complex workarounds that reduce code clarity and maintainability.      ### What did you expect to happen?  ## Expected Fix Nested helper functions should either: 1. Maintain access to the original root context via `$` even when parent context is overridden 2. Allow explicit root context passing that preserves the full Helm context object 3. Provide clear docum

title: Proposal: Add helm_rollback module to kubernetes.core
body: ### What would you like to be added?  ##### SUMMARY Problem: No rollback support in existing Helm module  The current Ansible module kubernetes.core.helm provides support for installing, upgrading, and removing Helm releases, but it does not provide an option for performing a Helm rollback.  Helm rollback is a fundamental Helm operation, widely used in CI/CD pipelines when a deployment fails or regressions appear. Because Ansible lacks this capability, users are forced to call the Helm CLI directly via command: or shell:, which makes automation inconsistent and breaks idempotent playbook design.  There is currently no Ansible-native way to roll back a Helm release using release revision history.  ##### ISSUE TYPE - Feature Idea  ##### COMPONENT NAME helm_rollback  ##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION  ##### Behavior:  Runs the equivalent of:  helm rollback <name> <revision> [-n namespace] [--wait] [--timeout X]   Always reports changed: true because rollback alters cluster state. body: ### What happened?  `Helm4` uses `operation: Update` in `managedFields` for new resources in helm releases. At the same time, k8s doc says this: ``` The field management record consists of basic information about the managing entity itself, plus details about the fields being managed and the relevant operation (Apply or Update). body: ### What happened?  Helm 4's `helm template` command defaults to Kubernetes 1.20 instead of matching the client-go version (currently 1.34). This causes charts that use `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` to render old/deprecated API versions.  Charts using capability detection (like Bitnami's common library) render `policy/v1beta1` instead of `policy/v1` for PodDisruptionBudgets, `batch/v1beta1` instead of `batch/v1` for CronJobs, etc.  **Root cause:** The `Makefile` (lines 70-71) has incorrect LDFLAGS paths. They target `helm.sh/helm/v4/pkg/chart/common/util.k8sVersionMajor` but the variables are actually in `pkg/chart/common/capabilities.go` (package `common`, not `common/util`). The LDFLAGS silently fail, leaving the hardcoded 1.20 defaults instead of the client-go version.  This was introduced in commit 9dcc49cbd "Move lint pkg to be part of each chart version".  ### What did you expect to happen?  `helm template` should default to the Kubernetes version matching the bundled client-go library (v0.34.x = K8s 1.34), allowing charts to render current stable API versions when no cluster is available or `--kube-version` is not specified.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  ```bash # Create test chart mkdir -p /tmp/testchart/templates cat > /tmp/testchart/Chart.yaml << 'EOF' apiVersion: v2 name: testchart version: 0.1.0 EOF  cat > /tmp/testchart/templates/test.yaml << 'EOF' KubeVersion: {{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion.Version }} Major: {{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion.Major }} Minor: {{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion.Minor }} EOF  # Test with no cluster access to force default capabilities KUBECONFIG=/dev/null helm template test /tmp/testchart ```  **Expected output:** ```yaml KubeVersion: v1.34.0 Major: 1 Minor: 34 ```  **Actual output:** ```yaml KubeVersion: v1.20.0 Major: 1 Minor: 20 ```  **Real-world impact test:** ```bash KUBECONFIG=/dev/null helm template test bitnami/keycloak --version 24.2.1 | grep -A2 "kind: PodDisruptionBudget" ```  Shows `a

title: Helm WASM Plugin Support for Custom Template Functions
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Helm should provide an **optional interface in Helm v4's Extism plugin runtime** that allows WASM plugins to register custom template functions directly into the templating system:[1]  - Add a plugin type (e.g., `wasm-template-functions`) that can expose additional template functions callable during chart rendering. - Security is governed by an **allowlist/denylist** for functions configured in `plugins.yaml`. - This system should support all Helm workflows (lint, template, install) without requiring wrapper binaries or external scripts. - The interface should be fully backward compatible, with plugins only enabled via opt-in configuration.  ### Why is this needed?  This extension is needed for the following reasons:[12138](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12138)  - **Streamlined CI/CD integration:** CI/CD systems require hooks for validation, reporting, and metric recording during chart rendering—not after. Post-renderers and getter plugins cannot provide context-aware, template-time logic. - **Extensible and language-agnostic:** WASM plugins allow registration of custom logic in any supported language, without modifying Helm core or tightly coupling to a specific version. - **Security and maintainability:** System administrators retain control over which functions are exposed, protecting against malicious templates and unexpected side-effects. - **Eliminates wrapper complexity:** Today, custom functions require wrapper programs around Helm, which breaks IDE integrations, increases complexity, and is fragile to Helm upgrades. - **Platform migration:** The same chart template works across environments—local development, Jenkins, CircleCI—by swapping plugins rather than rewriting chart logic. - **Developer experience:** Local plugins can provide dry-run behavior (log-only, no side effects), while production plugins can interact with external APIs securely. - **Early failure detection and richer error handling:** Template-time

title: Consider resources created in pre-install / pre-upgrade hook for adoption
body: ### What would you like to be added?  #### Proposal  I would like to propose that K8s resources created in Helm pre-install and pre-upgrade hook be considered for Helm adoption. Fundamentally, these resources should not be treated differently from resources that exist prior to  installing / upgrading the chart with adoption annotations and labels.  #### Why this doesn't work currently?  Prior to Helm install / upgrade, Helm collects matching resources in the environment that is declared in the manifest into `toBeAdopted` list. Resources created out-of-band do not contribute to the list. Therefore, when we proceed to updating the environment, Helm sees that a declared manifest is already in the environment but not in `toBeAdopted` list, so `original object <Kind> with the name <Name> not found` error is thrown ([ref](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/pkg/kube/client.go#L544-L548))  #### Additional Meta  I would like to add this to Helm v4 and backported to v3, which our production environment currently runs on if possible.  ### Why is this needed?  We're running proprietary software so I can't disclose the exact workflow that warrants pre-creating the resources, but I can imagine that this would not be uncommon. We can consider pre-creating the resources from our own operators ahead of Helm, but since these resources only make sense in a context of a Helm release, I would prefer if we can go with a first-class solution.

In `source-controller` we built a custom secure loader that addresses security needs from a Kubernetes controller perspective, e.g. confining the files available for being loaded as part of a chart under a given root path. To illustrate this, see how Helm upstream is loading charts:  ```go // Load takes a string name, tries to resolve it to a file or directory, and then loads it. // // This is the preferred way to load a chart. But .helmignore is not evaluated when reading out of an archive. func Load(name string) (chart.Charter, error) { 	l, err := Loader(name) 	if err != nil { 		return nil, err 	} 	return l.Load() } ```  And how Flux is doing the same:  ```go // Load takes a string root and name, tries to resolve it to a file or directory, // and then loads it securely without traversing outside of root. // // This is the preferred way to load a chart. Enhanced Flexibility: Enables new use cases where charts come from non-filesystem sources 4. Security Benefits: Reduces attack surface by avoiding temporary file creation, which can be important in multi-tenant environments. 5. Developer Experience: Provides a more intuitive API for developers working with charts in memory-mapped scenarios. 6. Consistency with Modern Practices: Many modern applications prefer in-memory processing for better performance and resource management.

Example:  ```yaml # Unreliable: the needed feature gate might be manually toggled by flag kubeVersion: ">=1.29.0"  # Better: the dependency on a particular feature gate is clearer kubeFeatureGates:   SidecarContainers: true ```  ### Why is this needed?  Firstly, thanks for reading.  As far as I can tell, the `kubeVersion` field is the closest thing in `Chart.yaml` to being able to ensure a particular feature gate is enabled. But the operators of a cluster can use the `--feature-gates` flag, so `kubeVersion` isn't foolproof. It'd be better for a chart to provide a set of required feature gates:  - so that installation can be blocked early on with a more semantic reason ("foo requires SidecarContainers, which is not enabled on this cluster") - charts could be allowed to install on lower k8s versions where the required feature gates are in alpha but manually enabled, rather than prevented by a k8s version comparison

title: Helm v4 SDK no longer offers the ability to specify a logger per action
body: ### What happened?  While testing Helm v4 SDK. One regression for us is the [inability to pass a custom logger ](https://pkg.go.dev/helm.sh/helm/v4@v4.0.0-alpha.1/pkg/action#Configuration.Init)to `action.Init` anymore. ([before](https://pkg.go.dev/helm.sh/helm/v3/pkg/action#Configuration.Init)).  I understand the change, but **it removes the SDK’s ability to easily attach specific log contexts per action**. At work, we enrich logs with request metadata before sending them via webhook or message queue, so each Helm action has properly scoped logs with a deployment id we provide. It works very well. I had started [implementing](https://github.com/helm/helm/commit/b642bca8f61dfbe19e98ad75b73b2eaac2511405) something similar when migrating parts of Helm to slog, but it was later removed. Still the regression is [my fault](https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/30708#issuecomment-2793640713). **Currently, the only way I see is through `slog.SetDefault(customLogger)`, which is global and can’t handle concurrent requests properly.**  It will be a regression for Flux too. See https://github.com/fluxcd/helm-controller/blob/de97aa9d843c2e9765de217470ba67195b5ce733/internal/action/config.go#L52  ### What did you expect to happen?  Be able to have a custom logger per action.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  It is via [SDK](https://github.com/helm/helm-www/blob/d44a2b4cf281b3863077fe74f0df4900ec061b93/sdkexamples/main.go#L38) but code will look like ```diff 	if err := actionConfig.Init( 		settings.RESTClientGetter(), 		namespace, 		helmDriver, -		logger.Printf); err != nil { +		); err != nil { 		return nil, err 	} ```  ### Helm version  <details>  ```console $ helm version v4 beta 1 ``` </details>   ### Kubernetes version  <details>  ```console $ kubectl version # paste output here ```  </details>

title: Feature Request:  Add Support for `--version latest` to Helm install command
body: ### What would you like to be added?  The Helm install command currently accepts a `--version` argument.  When specified, that argument identifies a specific version of the Helm chart to be installed.  When it is omitted, Helm installs the "latest" version of the Helm chart.  My suggestion is to add support for explicitly specifying `--version latest` to trigger the same behavior.  Note: I am not suggesting removing the current behavior, I am only suggesting an alternate argument combination for achieving the same thing.  ### Why is this needed?  This request comes out of developing deployment scripts using Helm.  The current Helm behavior requires checking whether the user has requested a specific version of a Helm chart and, if so, adding the `--version` argument with the requested version number.  That isn't difficult; but it would be cleaner/easier if we could always include the `--version` argument and set a default value of "latest" to the variable used for Helm chart version in our script.  If the user specifies a different version, it would override the default value and no conditional processing has to occur.  A potential objection someone might raise is: what if a Helm chart project chooses to use the same value ("latest") as the version number for a specific version of the chart AND that version that is not, in fact, the _latest_ version.  I'm not sure how to address that except to point out that the Helm documentation strongly encourages the use of SemVer2 version numbers.  I also suspect this issue is something of a red herring, but, if necessary, this proposal could adopt some other special value to represent "latest".

title: Add CLI command to generate values.schema.json from values.yaml
body: Currently, Helm supports validating values against a values.schema.json, but there is no built-in way to generate such a schema from values.yaml. Chart maintainers often rely on third-party tools like [helm-schema-gen](https://github.com/karuppiah7890/helm-schema-gen).  Proposal: Introduce a new Helm CLI command (or flag), for example: ``` helm schema generate values.yaml [flags] ``` This would:  - Parse the provided values.yaml. - Generate a draft values.schema.json with inferred types (string, number, boolean, array, object). - Optionally include comments from values.yaml as "description" fields in the schema. - Provide a --strict or --loose mode to control how aggressively types are inferred.  ### Why is this needed?  - Improve developer experience for chart maintainers. - Reduce reliance on external tools for something that feels like core Helm functionality. - Encourage wider adoption of schema validation in charts by lowering the barrier to entry.

title: detect if helm is running in template mode (for generating static YAML)
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Expose a new [built-in object](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/builtin_objects/) that indicates the mode Helm is running in, e.g. "normal" mode (`helm install` or `helm upgrade`) vs template-only mode (`helm template`).    ### Why is this needed?  I have a maybe slightly creative use-case: I want to use `helm template` to produce a YAML manifest for a [static pod](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/static-pod/) , to be installed by the user in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ on the k8s nodes, _not_ to send to the k8s API.  A common installation pattern for some apps is to either deploy a daemonset (via the k8s API), or YAML manifests for static pods in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ on k8s nodes.  So I could have a Helm value like `installationMethod`  which could be e.g. `daemonSet` or `staticPod` to control which files in the chart `templates/` directory are activated.  The thing is, if you `helm install` rather than `helm template` with `installationMethod: staticPod`, Helm will install a static pod via the k8s API which is not the desired result. So preferably I could check and fail if helm is running in "actually talk to the API mode" instead of "template mode".   Or does anyone have another better suggestion to reach the same goal?  Thanks!

title: Helm signing doesn't work if an ed25519 key exists in the keyring even if you're signing with an RSA key

title: x/crypto/openpgp is deprecated since 2021 we should find alternative libraries for signing
body: ### What would you like to be added?  This was brought up in https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/11634 , and I also came across some messaging about this package being deprecated while I was investigating another issue with the openpgp golang library.  https://github.com/golang/go/issues/44226 https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp  > Deprecated: this package is unmaintained except for security fixes. New applications should consider a more focused, modern alternative to OpenPGP for their specific task  I would suggest we add support for a different library for Helm v4 if possible.  This could be an interface where one implementation is openpgp , and another could be added alongside it, or a replacement entirely.  ### Why is this needed?  Since there are no longer any changes (aside from security fixes) to the golang library for openpgp: - If there are any changes in the default ways people create keys or store their keyring, the `--sign` functionality will not work for those users. One example of this is how people have been more commonly using ed25519 keys. - If GPG has changes in different OS distributions, this could also break the openpgp library.  - This impacts new helm functionality being added such as [Helm Plugin Signing](https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/31176).

I've seen many devs which are struggeling with the templating features, which result in quite complex helm charts for very simple applications. This is very often a topic for inhouse applications. Usually inhouse applications in larger organisations, simply want to switch some variables and the ingress between the stages dev, uat, prod,..  The different layers of applying and mapping variabes are confusing sometimes: - configmap/secret - values.yaml - values-stage.yaml - command line argument(s) With the variable replacement in helm, it's not always obvious what they deploy. And people find real complex solutions for simple problems then 😺  Having this feature, it would be much easier for people to check the configuration and apply hotfixes. Also simple deployment configurations could be managed via kustomize overlays and got managed through helm. And it would benefit from the advanced lifecycle management.  The dev's I've spoken to love to simply uninstall apps and reinstall them in dev environments, if they've broken something.

title: Regression: Helm v3.18.5 no longer accepts typed arrays as values when invoked via API
body: ### What happened?  When invoking an `Install` or `Upgrade` action via the API with an array value passed as a typed object, the validation fails with: ``` test-chart: - at '/dummies': invalid jsonType []map[string]interface {} ```  This happens if the array was given as a Go array-of-objects (`[]map[string]any`): ``` _, err = installAction.Run(chart, map[string]any{ 	// Use of map[string]any (array-of-objects) causes validation to fail! 	"dummies": []map[string]any{ 		{ 			"foo": 1, 			"bar": "test-value", 		}, 	}, }) ```  If I convert the dummies array into an untyped array (`[]any`) first, then validation passes as expected: ``` _, err = installAction2.Run(chart, map[string]any{ 	// Here, dummies is an untyped array of any, and now validation succeeds. 	"dummies": []any{ 		map[string]any{ 			"foo": 1, 			"bar": "test-value", 		}, 	}, }) ```  I believe this happens because v3.18.5 switched the JSON validation library, which is stricter about the types that it accepts. Specifically, the implementation of its `typeOf()` only accepts untyped arrays (`[]any`), but not arrays that have a stronger type specified. See here: https://github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/blob/32784e992ee32ae73891b165b1319dd0bca87437/schema.go#L128  ### What did you expect to happen?  I was expecting the typed arrays to also work as values (e.g., `[]map[string]any`), as they did in v3.18.4.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  Here's a minimal repro project: [jsonvalidation_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21836184/jsonvalidation_repro.zip)  Just unzip this somewhere and run with `go run .`  ### Helm version  Applies to Helm v3.18.5, but only when invoked via the Go API. I don't think this can be reproduced using the Helm binary because of how it handles the values files.  This is a regression in v3.18.5, as v3.18.4 did not have this issue.  ### Kubernetes version  Not relevant. Reproduces without Kubernetes.

title: Regression: Helm 3.18.5 rejects JSON Schema $ref URLs that worked in 3.17.x
body: ### What happened?  After upgrading runners to Helm 3.18.5, `helm upgrade` began failing schema validation for charts that reference remote JSON Schemas over HTTPS in values.schema.json  Example error: ``` Error: UPGRADE FAILED: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s): my-app: failing loading "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema/master/v1.24.0-standalone-strict/podsecuritycontext.json": invalid file url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema/master/v1.24.0-standalone-strict/podsecuritycontext.json ```  The same charts and values validate and upgrade successfully with Helm 3.17.4.  ### What did you expect to happen?  `helm upgrade` should continue to accept the same values.schema.json patterns that worked in 3.17.x  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  Chart layout (minimal): ``` mychart/   Chart.yaml   values.yaml   values.schema.json ```  values.schema.json ``` {   "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema",   "type": "object",   "properties": {     "podSecurityContext": {       "$ref": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema/master/v1.24.0-standalone-strict/podsecuritycontext.json"     }   } } ```  Run ``` helm upgrade test ./mychart --install ```  ### Helm version  <details> This was observed on Github Actions:  ``` Installing v3.18.5   Downloading 'v3.18.5' from 'https://get.helm.sh/' ``` </details>   ### Kubernetes version  <details>  Not relevant  </details>

title: Removing subchart value via override results in warning
body: ### What happened?  If I have a chart ("Parent Chart"), which has a dependency on another chart ("Child Chart"), and I define some a dictionary value for Child Chart in Parent Chart's `values.yaml`, if I then attempt to remove this dictionary value (by setting to `null`) will result in 2 (duplicate) warnings.  For example, if I define the `resources` for the Child chart in Parent's `values.yaml`: ``` child-chart:   resources:     limits:       cpu: 100m       memory: 128Mi     requests:       cpu: 100m       memory: 128Mi ```  If I then try to remove the `resouces`, e.g. via `--set child-chart.resources=null`, the following warnings are reported: ``` coalesce.go:298: warning: cannot overwrite table with non table for subchart-test.child-chart.resources (map[limits:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi] requests:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi]]) coalesce.go:298: warning: cannot overwrite table with non table for subchart-test.child-chart.resources (map[limits:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi] requests:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi]]) ```  The same errors occur if the removal is done via a 2nd values file (`--values values.yaml,values-override.yaml`).  The end result is as expected (the Child Chart does not have resource limits), but a sufficiently large parent chart can result in a lot of these warnings.   Interestingly, if you take the sub-chart out of the equation, and attempt to do the same on the parent chart, no warnings are logged - this only occurs when doing it on a child chart.  ### What did you expect to happen?  No warning logged  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  1. Check out the example chart at https://github.com/bpfoster/helm-subchart-warning-example 2. Run `helm template --set child-chart.resources=null --set resources=null .` 3. Observe warnings on child-chart: ``` coalesce.go:298: warning: cannot overwrite table with non table for parent-chart.child-chart.resources (map[limits:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi] requests:map[cpu:100m memory:128Mi]])

title: Support for write only argument as `repository_password_wo` attribute in helm_release
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Add support for a [write only argument](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework/resources/write-only-arguments) for the `repository_password` attribute in helm_release as `repository_password_wo` with `repository_password_wo_version`.  ### Why is this needed?  Currently, there is no way of supplying the `repository_password` attribute without its value being stored in the state file. Adding a write only argument version of this attribute will enable users to use this attribute without it having to be stored in the state file enhancing security of the helm_release resource.

title: Helm allows installing a chart using invalid YAML in values.yaml

title: ConfigMap with `helm.sh/hook` annotation is deleted during first helm upgrade
body: ### What happened?  I have a Helm chart with a Deployment, Service, and a ConfigMap. I needed to add a Job to perform a database migration, so I added Helm hook annotations to both the Job and the ConfigMap.  I added the following annotations to the ConfigMap: ``` annotations:   "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade   "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-100" ```  When I run `helm upgrade` for the first time after adding these annotations, Helm deletes the ConfigMap during the upgrade process. If I run `helm upgrade` again, the ConfigMap is created properly and is no longer deleted. If I run `helm install` where hook is added from the beginning, the ConfigMap isn't deleted either.  This behavior is unexpected. According to Helm documentation, hook resources shouldn't be removed like this unless explicitly marked with `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy`, which I did not set.  ### What did you expect to happen?  The ConfigMap with hook annotations should be updated without unexpected delete during the first helm upgrade.  ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  1. title: Add --show-resource-errors flag to display kubectl events and pod logs when atomic operations fail
body: ### What would you like to be added?  Add a new flag `--show-resource-errors` to `helm install` and `helm upgrade` commands that works in conjunction with `--atomic` to automatically capture and display Kubernetes events and pod logs when a deployment fails.  The flag would: - Only activate when used together with `--atomic` - Capture Kubernetes warning events from the deployment - Show pod statuses and container error states - Display container logs from failed pods - Output error details to stderr before the atomic rollback/uninstall occurs  Example usage: ```bash helm upgrade --install myapp ./chart --atomic --show-resource-errors ```  ### Why is this needed?  When using `helm upgrade --install --atomic` and the deployment fails, Helm automatically rolls back (on upgrade) or uninstalls (on install) the release. However, users are left without visibility into what actually went wrong during the deployment attempt.  Currently, when an atomic operation fails, users see only a generic error message like: ``` Error: release my-app failed, and has been uninstalled due to atomic being set: timed out waiting for the condition ```  To debug the issue, users must: 1. Quickly run `kubectl get events` before resources are cleaned up 2. Try to capture pod logs with `kubectl logs` 3. Check pod statuses and container states 4. Often miss critical information because resources are already deleted  This creates several problems: - **Lost debugging information**: By the time users run kubectl commands, the failed resources are often already cleaned up - **Poor developer experience**: Users must scramble to capture error details before they disappear - **Increased debugging time**: Without immediate error visibility, troubleshooting takes significantly longer - **Repeated failures**: Without understanding why deployments fail, users often retry with the same issues  With the proposed `--show-resource-errors` flag, users would get immediate visibility into failure reasons: ``` Error

title: Add optional color support to Helm CLI output
body: ### What would you like to be added?  I’d like to introduce **optional ANSI color support** to Helm CLI output via a `--color` flag. This would help users visually distinguish important elements such as:  * Status labels (e.g., `deployed`, `failed`) * Section headers (e.g., `REVISION`, `NAMESPACE`) * Contextual metadata like release names or ports  The colorization should:  * Be opt-in (disabled by default) * Detect if output is interactive (`isatty`) and disable colors in non-TTY contexts like piping to a file * Be applied conservatively to avoid disrupting scripting/parsing  The implementation will leverage existing dependencies like [fatih/color](https://github.com/fatih/color), already vendored in Helm.   A working prototype is being prepared locally and could be contributed as a reference implementation. The changes are confined to output formatting in selected commands such as:  * `helm status` * `helm list` * `helm install`  I’d be happy to move this into a formal [HIP](https://github.com/helm/community/tree/main/hips) if maintainers see value in this idea.  ### Why is this needed?  Colorful CLI output is standard in many popular DevOps tools (e.g., `kubectl`, `docker`, `git`, `terraform`). Adding color support will:  * Improve human readability and focus during CI/CD or release debugging * Enhance developer experience when interpreting Helm output * Enable terminal themes or UI-based Helm wrappers to parse visual cues more easily  Since Helm often outputs logs, ports, and resource status, making these visually distinct helps developers debug and understand the state of their deployments faster.  This would align Helm with modern CLI UX practices while preserving backward compatibility for pipelines and machine parsing.

title: Helm's CRD upgrade behavior frustrates users, is a production time bomb, and discourages good testing practices
body: ### What would you like to be added?  The "safety feature" of helm ignoring CRD changes during an upgrade, with silent success of the upgrade if CRD has changed, and no means for a user to override this behavior, results in (likely unintended) **unsafe** side-effects: - Controllers silently fail in production at some point in the future (the "time bomb") as they try to access presumed new, renamed, or removed fields in a stale CRD. Developers/DevOps have to deal with this extra frustration, having to realize their CRD did not get upgraded in the cluster and "fight the system" when it would be perfectly fine to upgrade them in 90% of cases (#5853, #11137, #11969, #12596). - During development, dealing with helm's refusal to force CRD application is infuriating: having to blow away the cluster or do a full `helm uninstall` each testing cycle slows down development/testing cycles, consumes developers' time, and discourages test-driven development that is already expensive due to the integrated nature of kubernetes.  The upgrade behavior of helm should be changed such that: 1. If there are any **new** (non-existent in the cluster) or **modified** (different from those in the cluster with the same name) CRDs in the chart, helm should:   - if feasible, check if the **changed** CRDs follow [kubernetes' CRD versioning practices](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definition-versioning/), and automatically apply such versioned CRDs without user intervention;   - immediately **abort** the upgrade with an error **listing the changed CRDs that require manual upgrade** before the upgrade can proceed.   - if we get past the first two bullet points, **apply any new CRDs automatically**. 2. allow the user to provide a flag such as `--force-crds` or similar, that will force helm to apply the CRDs, which would be useful in two scenarios:   - development/testing cycle;   - application to a production cluster when the upgrade has already

title: Helm fails on valid SemVer dependency version when pre-release starts with '0f' (e.g. 0.0.1-0f9a5fdef.38)
body: What happened?  Helm fails to accept a dependency version such as `0.0.1-0f9a5fdef.38` (pre-release starting with `0f`), even though it is valid according to [SemVer 2.0.0](https://semver.org/#spec-item-9).  **Error Example:** ``` Error: dependency "ram-my-charts" has an invalid version/constraint format: improper constraint: 0.0.0.1-4e43d1a30.5f9a5fdef.38 ``` - The error message shows the version string is being mangled (extra zero/dot is added). - If the pre-release starts with a letter (e.g. `0.0.1-b95cec4ab.38`), or a digit (e.g. `0.0.1-485ca4b.38`, `0.0.1-07c062a.38`), it works fine. - If the pre-release starts with `0f` (zero followed by "f"), it consistently fails.  What did you expect to happen?  - Helm should allow pre-release identifiers that start with `0f...` as per the SemVer spec. - No error should be thrown for valid version strings.  How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?  1. In your `Chart.yaml` or `requirements.yaml`, add a dependency like:     ```yaml     dependencies:       - name: ram-my-charts         version: 0.0.1-0f9a5fdef.38         repository: "https://example.com/charts"     ``` 2. Run `helm dependency update` or any Helm operation that resolves dependencies. 3. Try other versions like `0.0.1-485ca4b.38`, `0.0.1-07c062a.38` (these work), and compare.  Where the Issue Occurs  - File: `pkg/downloader/manager.go` - Line: The call to `semver.NewConstraint(dep.Version)` in `downloadAll()` and `tarFromLocalDir()` is where the error is raised.   ```go   constraint, err := semver.NewConstraint(dep.Version) // <--- error is thrown here   ``` - The root cause appears to be upstream of this call: the version string is mangled (an extra zero or dot is introduced) before being passed to `semver.NewConstraint`.  Scenario  - Dependency version: `0.0.1-0f9a5fdef.38` (fails) - Dependency version: `0.0.1-b95cec4ab.38` (works) - Dependency version: `0.0.1-485ca4b.38` (works) - Dependency version: `0.0.1-07c062a.38` (works) - Lock

title: Support a global plugins directory
body: For system package managers it would be nice when `helm` would support a global plugins directory by default. For example the `HELM_PLUGINS` variable could default to `$HOME/.local/share/helm/plugins:/usr/share/helm/plugins`. If altering the default `HELM_PLUGINS` variable is the solution to go, the issue #11310 must be fixed beforehand.

title: index concurrency issue
body: When running helm dependency build concurrently (e.g., in CI/CD systems like Argo CD), Helm often fails with errors like: ``` Error: error loading /helm-workdir/repository/helmize-index.yaml: empty index.yaml file helm.go:92: 2025-06-15 13:38:10.255000423 +0000 UTC m=+0.444128126 [debug] empty index.yaml file helm.sh/helm/v3/pkg/repo.init ```  This happens because multiple helm processes are trying to download index.yaml at the same time. Helm currently has no concurrency protection around these operations.  Context:  We observed this issue while deploying Helm-based applications at scale with Argo CD. In our setup: * We have up to 70 parallel helm dependency build processes triggered * When using the official Helm binary, many of these processes fail with filesystem-related errors * This affects Argo CD users heavily, especially when using a shared HELM_CACHE_HOME * index.yaml file has a size of about 30MB * this behavior can occur on heavily loaded disk spaces  Reproduction Steps:  We created a test setup that: * Launches 250 parallel helm dependency build commands (each in its own working directory but using shared Helm cache). * With the upstream Helm binary, the test at least once fails due to race conditions on downloading & writing index.yaml directory.  The patch was tested under the same conditions (250 parallel helm dependency build), and no failures occurred.  Log test without lock files (in attaches): [without-lock-test.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20749910/without-lock-test.log) Log test with lock files (in attaches): [with-lock-test.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20749911/with-lock-test.log) You can see the test script [here](https://github.com/fm1ck3y/helm/tree/bug/repo-concurrency/tests)   Would Helm maintainers consider merging support for optional file-based locking to mitigate concurrency issues?   We're happy to contribute our patch via PR with proper tests if this direction is acceptable.  Related Issues: * http

title: Regression on OCI auth mechanism for GCP
body: Before `3.18` and still mentioned in the documentation https://helm.sh/docs/topics/registries/#oci-feature-deprecation-and-behavior-changes-with-v380 > The helm registry login command now follows the same structure as the Docker CLI for storing credentials. The same location for registry configuration can be passed to both Helm and the Docker CLI.  Helm and Docker used to share the credentials configuration, and the documentation on GCP (https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication#methods) used to be valid to pull from Artifact Registry (Helm using the Docker config, where the GCP Docker credential helper https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr is configured, and credentials are automatically provided).  ``` cat ~/.docker/config.json { 	"credHelpers": { 		"asia.gcr.io": "gcloud", 		"eu.gcr.io": "gcloud", 		"europe-docker.pkg.dev": "gcloud", 		"gcr.io": "gcloud", 		"marketplace.gcr.io": "gcloud", 		"staging-k8s.gcr.io": "gcloud", 		"us.gcr.io": "gcloud" 	} } ```  This is not the case anymore, now we need to manually provide the token credentials every time we log in to GCP.  ``` gcloud auth print-access-token | helm registry login -u oauth2accesstoken --password-stdin europe-docker.pkg.dev ```

title: Helm OCI auth change in 3.18.x
body: ORAS v1 used POST for auth as part of OAuth workflow ORAS v2 changed to GET for this  While this does not affect most users, the change has caused a regression in at least one custom registry that relied on checking the POST auth request. That registry has since updated it's implementation of both—legitimate—auth options, but this is still considered a regression since functionality has changed.  Note that the auth flow was not well-documented in the docker implementation used by ORAS 1, but it is well-documented in the ORAS 2 OCI auth implementation: https://github.com/opencontainers/wg-auth/blob/main/docs/implementations/ORAS.md?plain=1  Also see: - #30950 (closed)  - #30967

title: Create OCI Registry Compatibility Matrix
body: The Open Container Initiative (OCI) [distribution-spec](https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec) defines an API protocol to standardize the distribution of content. However, registry providers have often either extended or customized the baseline specification to serve their needs. The differences between each registry implementation becomes a challenge to ensure conformance and provide a seamless end user experience for those storing and managing Helm charts within these systems.  Create a compatibility matrix with the major OCI Image registry providers using a set of automated tooling to confirm that Helm complies with these target systems.  1. Determine list of registry providers 2. Determine activities that should be used to confirm conformance 3. Develop automated testing 4. Publish conformance matrix

title: Clean Separation between CLI/Client and SDK
body: While Helm has a client and SDK, the separate between them isn't clean. For example, the SDK assumes OCI credentials come from files it should read and does not provide a way for an application to pass those into the SDK. There are many examples of this lack of separation throughout the codebase.  This issue is to track having a clean separation.

title: Spurious warnings when parent and dependency charts have different types for the same value
body: I have a chart that has a dependency on the [bitnami rabbitmq chart](https://github.com/bitnami/charts/tree/main/bitnami/rabbitmq), and I'm getting a spurious warning about a "non-table value".  After a bit of digging I have reduced the example down to the following:  **Chart.yaml** ```yaml apiVersion: v2 name: test-chart description: Chart to demonstrate spurious warnings type: application version: 0.1.0 appVersion: "0.1"  dependencies:   - name: rabbitmq     version: 15.x.x     repository: oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts ```  **values.yaml** ```yaml ingress:   enabled: true   tls:     host: host.example.com ```  (plus any template, I've just used one that renders `{{ .Values | toYaml }}` to show the final merged values).  Running this chart with `helm template` gives:  ``` coalesce.go:301: warning: destination for rabbitmq.ingress.tls is a table.
