Running helm under a debugger I see that the warning message is being printed when helm is exploring the dependency tree, and seems to be trying to coalesce the _top level_ chart values with those of the rabbitmq _subchart_. title: `helm uninstall --wait` Lacks Detailed Feedback When Stuck on Resource Deletion
body: When `helm uninstall <release> --wait --timeout <duration>` runs, and it gets stuck because a Kubernetes resource isn't deleting, it's hard to tell *which* resource is causing the problem. The command just hangs until the timeout, then fails. It would be much more helpful if Helm could provide more information about what it's waiting for during that period.  I'm using Helm in an automation script to install and uninstall applications like Longhorn and Fission. Sometimes, during an uninstall, a resource (like a pod with a stuck volume mount, or a CR with a finalizer that won't release) doesn't terminate quickly. When this happens, `helm uninstall --wait` just sits there. My script has to guess what's wrong, or i have to manually run a bunch of `kubectl get pods -n <namespace> --watch` or `kubectl describe <kind> <name> -n <namespace>` commands in another terminal to find the stuck resource.  Right now, my workaround is to not always use `--wait` in the script for uninstalls where i anticipate problems, and instead implement my own polling logic with `kubectl` to check if all resources from the release are gone. Or, i just let `helm uninstall --wait` timeout and then manually debug. This makes the automation less reliable and harder to debug when it fails.  If `helm uninstall --wait` could be improved, it would simplify things a lot. For example, if it's waiting for resources to be deleted, it could periodically print which resources are still present or still in a terminating state. This would give immediate feedback to the user or the automation script about what's holding up the uninstall.  I think this would be useful for many people, not just me. Anyone who uses `helm uninstall --wait` for complex applications that might have resources with finalizers, persistent volume claims, or other dependencies could run into this. When an uninstall hangs, knowing *which* of the possibly dozens of resources is the culprit saves a lot of time. It makes Helm more user-friendly

title: BA2001: LoadImageAboveFourGigabyteAddress reported by BinSkim 4.41
body: The latest version of [BinSkim](https://github.com/microsoft/binskim) (4.4.1) is reporting a [BA2001](https://github.com/microsoft/binskim/blob/main/docs/BinSkimRules.md#rule-ba2001loadimageabovefourgigabyteaddress) error with `helm.exe` that poses a potential security issue.  The issue exists in the latest 3.18.0 (download [here](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v3.18.0-windows-amd64.zip)) version of the binary and prior versions.  > 64-bit images should have a preferred base address above the 4GB boundary to prevent triggering an Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) compatibility mode that decreases security. ASLR compatibility mode reduces the number of locations to which ASLR may relocate the binary, reducing its effectiveness at mitigating memory corruption vulnerabilities. To resolve this issue, either use the default preferred base address by removing any uses of /baseaddress from compiler command lines, or /BASE from linker command lines (recommended), or configure your program to start at a base address above 4GB when compiled for 64 bit platforms (by changing the constant passed to /baseaddress or /BASE). Note that if you choose to continue using a custom preferred base address, you will need to make this modification only for 64-bit builds, as base addresses above 4GB are not valid for 32-bit binaries. For VC projects make sure that ItemDefinitionGroup - Link - BaseAddress property is not set.  To reproduce the result locally, you can refer to [this](https://github.com/microsoft/binskim?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-extract-the-exe-file-from-the-nuget-package) and the [user guide](https://github.com/microsoft/binskim/blob/main/docs/UserGuide.md).  The specific command I ran to reproduce this was: ``` .\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BinSkim.4.4.1\tools\net9.0\win-x64\BinSkim.exe analyze .\helm.3.18.0\windows-amd64\helm.exe ```

title: Run Helm unit-tests with `-shuffle=on` and `-count=n` (n > 1)
body: `go test` by default runs unit tests once in a deterministic order.  Leading to: 1. deterministic order: tests relying on their order of execution to pass 2. running once: higher probability of flakey tests passing  Helm's unit tests have encountered both problems lately. Tests relying on running in a particular order, or being flakey.  Adding `-shuffle=on` and `-count=n` (for `n > 1`; perhaps 2 or 3, TBD) will improve these behaviors:  > -count n 	    Run each test, benchmark, and fuzz seed n times (default 1). 	    If -cpu is set, run n times for each GOMAXPROCS value. 	    Examples are always run once. -count does not apply to 	    fuzz tests matched by -fuzz.  > -shuffle off,on,N 	    Randomize the execution order of tests and benchmarks. 	    It is off by default. If -shuffle is set to on, then it will seed 	    the randomizer using the system clock. If -shuffle is set to an 	    integer N, then N will be used as the seed value. In both cases, 	    the seed will be reported for reproducibility.  https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go/internal/test

title: `restartPolicy = OnFailure` and non-0 `backoffLimit` causes `--wait-for-jobs` to not function correctly upon Job failure
body: ## Context  I am using Helm to deploy a Chart by running `helm install` inside CI. The Helm chart contains a Job and several other resources (such as Deployments). This Job is **not** a Helm hook. I would like the `helm install` and the `helm upgrade` commands to wait until the Job reaches the `Completed` or the `Failed` state. If the Job fails, then I would also like the Helm command to exit with an error code, thus signaling to CI that something went wrong.  While working with a chart recently, I noticed that when the Job has `restartPolicy` set to `OnFailure`, the `backoffLimit` is more than 0, and the Job fails to succeed, Helm waits indefinitely; instead of exiting immediately with a non-0 return code.  I looked at some issues that were related to `--wait-for-jobs` but none of them highlight this particular case (https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9285, https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/13757, https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/30533).  The existing patch https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/11289 attempts to move the implementation of `isReady` away from pod counters, and I wonder if it will fix this issue. ### Possible Root Cause  I believe that this is related to this section of [`ready.go`](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/46e79be5ebcff2658e7c048c3d6fb31d086c048e/pkg/kube/ready.go#L233-L245):  ```go if job.Status.Failed > *job.Spec.BackoffLimit {   slog.Debug("Job is failed", "namespace", job.GetNamespace(), "name", job.GetName())   // If a job is failed, it can't recover, so throw an error   return false, fmt.Errorf("job is failed: %s/%s", job.GetNamespace(), job.GetName()) } ```  The number of pods in the `Failed` connected to this Job never go above 1 because the `restartPolicy` is set to `OnFailure`, which means that pods are deleted, and a new one is created whenever a single attempt of the job fails. title: Helm dependency resolution failure for same chart names but from different repositories
body: ### Problem Description When a Helm chart declares multiple dependencies with the same name but from different repositories, dependency resolution fails. For example:  ```yaml dependencies: - name: common-chart   alias: common-chart   repository: '@repo1'   version: 1.0.0 - name: common-chart   alias: common-chart-alt   repository: '@repo2'     version: 2.0.0 ```  In this case, Helm incorrectly tries to resolve both dependencies using only one of the repositories, leading to errors like:  ``` Error: can't get a valid version for 1 subchart(s): "common-chart" (repository "https://repo2-url", version "1.0.0"). Make sure a matching chart version exists in the repo, or change the version constraint in Chart.yaml ```  ### Impact This limitation prevents legitimate use cases such as: - Using the same chart from different repositories with aliases - Developing against both production and development versions of a dependency - Using forks of the same chart for different environments  ### Analyse I think that the core problem lies in how Helm identifies and indexes dependencies during the resolution process.  In the resolveRepoNames function, a map (reposMap) is created that maps dependency names to repository names. This map uses only the dependency name as a key (`reposMap[dd.Name] = repo.Name`). When multiple dependencies have the same name but use different repositories, each subsequent dependency overwrites the previous one in this map. Later in the Resolve function, `repoName := repoNames[d.Name]` is used to look up the correct repository, but because there is only one entry per name, some dependencies get assigned to the wrong repository.  I think this explains why multiple dependencies with the same name cause problems: the last dependency with that name overwrites all previous ones in the map.  ### Proposed Solution Create composite keys that uniquely identify each dependency using name, repository, and index. title: `helm template --output-dir` should include all templates from the chart, even if empty
body: When running `helm template` with the `--output-dir` flag, Helm will only write templated files that aren't empty.  For example, running `helm template` for https://github.com/helm/helm/tree/9aefd2b32809960203d0178c89522f6bf3d4af9f/pkg/action/testdata/charts/chart-with-uncompressed-dependencies/charts/mariadb may not create [`secrets.yaml`](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/9aefd2b32809960203d0178c89522f6bf3d4af9f/pkg/action/testdata/charts/chart-with-uncompressed-dependencies/charts/mariadb/templates/secrets.yaml) in the output dir since the entire template is guarded by a conditional.  This is an issue for using Helm in [Bazel rules](https://bazel.build/versions/7.3.0/extending/rules?hl=en) (see https://github.com/abrisco/rules_helm/ for one example of using Helm in Bazel) since rules need to declare all output files that will be created and invocations of the rule will fail if not all files are written. Ideally, Helm will still write the template with the `# Source: <chart>/templates/...` even if the file is functionally empty (contains no resources).

title: Feature Request: JSON Schema Template Function
body: Hello, I've been working on a library chart and how it's used by applications, and we want to enforce JSON schema on library templates. Namely, I would like schemas to be contained in the library (as a subchart) instead of the application (as a parent chart), for library-owned template calls. This would allow us to most easily apply schema validation on our library template functions declaratively, which has added bonuses for making it much easier to document with something like https://github.com/CesiumGS/wetzel. It's true that we can check types imperatively but for templates that may be taking in complex nested objects, these imperative checks become significant areas of bloat and that bloat carries a higher risk of bugs.  The solution I would have in mind is some template function like `validateJsonSchema` which takes in 2-3 arguments: * schema[str/object?]: The json schema to validate against * object[object] The object to validate * fail_fast[bool] (default=True): Whether to invoke a failing function And it returns whether the schema passes or not. If fail=True, it wouldn't return, it would fail fast.  There could be other abstract ways to reach the same goal of mine (perhaps in a way that would encourage even better template function design).

title: Helm "managed by" metadata applied on every upgrade for custom resources
body: ## Description When `upgrading`, Helm appears to always attempt resource adoption of custom resources in the chart by patching the following metadata onto the resource: ```yaml annotations:   meta.helm.sh/release-name: "some-release"   meta.helm.sh/release-namespace: "some-namespace" labels:   app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: "Helm" ``` This happens despite there not actually being any material difference since the previous revision and also despite the fact that the resource on the cluster currently already has the metadata applied.  ## Impact This creates additional load on the k8s master by having to process these requests and run any admission validation/mutation that is attached to the resource. Overall making for a busier cluster.  ## Expected behaviour The manifest will contain this metadata and therefore will be correctly detected as not requiring a merge by the two way merge logic. This would also make the manifests more accurately reflect what helm applied to the cluster.  ## Additional Thoughts - On face value it would seem that this is caused due to the fact that this metadata does not end up in the generated manifests (e.g looking at the manifests for previous revisions this metadata is not present). The thinking here is that when it comes time for helm to diff it will always see a difference. - I believe that this does not happen for core resources due to the fact that core resources participate in three-way-merge, and therefore detect that the metadata is already applied by looking at the cluster, whereas CR's do not. https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9937

title: YAML parse errors should report the offending YAML
body: The Internet is quite filled with people who struggle to debug YAML parsing issues encountered by Helm.  The official guidance in the documentation is to... comment things out in order to view the rendered output (https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/debugging/). Apart from that people generally suggest to keep removing lines until the error goes away in an attempt to bisect the issue.  > When your YAML is failing to parse, but you want to see what is generated, one easy way to retrieve the YAML **is to comment out the problem section in the template**, and then re-run helm install --dry-run --debug:  The root cause for these attempts at workarounds is of course Helm's insufficient error messages in these cases.  Whenever Helm spits out an error such as  ``` Error: YAML parse error on somewhere/templates/something.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON: line 451: mapping values are not allowed in this context  Use --debug flag to render out invalid YAML ```  it is misleading users in two ways:  - The error is not actually in the specified file, nor on that line. In most cases, the line number won't even exist in the given file. That's of course because the error is in the interpolated template. - The --debug flag does not actually render the invalid YAML. It only adds a Helm-internal stack trace, which is irrelevant to debugging this issue:     ```    Error: YAML ...    helm.go:84: [debug] error converting YAML to JSON     helm.sh/helm/v3/pkg/.. < go stacktrace goes here >    ```  When Helm fails to parse some YAML, it should simply output (at the latest when --debug is specified) the actual data it failed to parse. That would greatly simplify debugging Helm templating issues. It is genuinely surprising Helm is not doing so. By way of analogy, the behavior of Helm here is similar to a C compiler which refers all error messages and line numbers to files _after_ running them through the pre-processor, but refuses to output the pre-processor result.

title: helm upgrade with updated HPA minReplicas returns before scaled pods are ready
body: When updating the minReplicas field in a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) via helm upgrade, Helm completes successfully (even with --wait) before the new minimum number of pods are created and become Ready. This can lead to situations where dependent systems or checks assume the upgrade is complete while pods are still pending.  **Expected behavior** When using helm upgrade --wait, Helm should ideally wait until the Deployment(s) associated with the HPA have scaled up to match the new minReplicas and all pods are in a Ready state before reporting success.  **Steps to reproduce**  Deploy a Helm chart that includes a Deployment and an HPA with minReplicas: 2.  Run helm upgrade with a values file that changes minReplicas: 5.  Observe that Helm reports success before the additional pods are created and ready.  Run kubectl get pods and see that not all 5 pods are ready yet.

title: Values from arguments merge strategy different from merge strategy onto default values.yaml
body: Hello, this is maybe even not a bug but certainly a strange quirk that caused me headaches this week. I eventually found the issue, where say you have a chart with default `values.yaml`. If you want values from `--set` (and others) to merge with `values.yaml`, it behaves differently than if you were to run `--values=./values.yaml`. It surely seems related to how just generally it's not obvious how arrays should merge with other arrays, compared to dictionaries where merging behavior is fairly obvious.  A pretty minimal chart shows this, consider: ```yaml # cat values.yaml ingresses: - fqdn: example.local   path: '/*' ```  ```yaml # $ cat templates/show.yaml spec:   {{- range .Values.ingresses }}   - fqdn: {{ .fqdn }}     path: {{ .path }}   {{- end }} ```  This `values.yaml` is the defaults, I wouldn't expect that applying `--values=./values.yaml` would be any different than just using the defaults. However, this discrepancy is exactly what happens.  Compare how these outputs are not the same, and the only difference in the command is `--values=./values.yaml`: ```shell $ helm template . --set ingresses[0].fqdn=example2.local --- # Source: helm-quirk/templates/show.yaml spec:   - fqdn: example2.local     path: ``` is different than ```shell $ helm template . --values=values.yaml --set ingresses[0].fqdn=example2.local --- # Source: helm-quirk/templates/show.yaml spec:   - fqdn: example2.local     path: /* ```  This directly is not that critical of a bug. Perhaps though it could uncover other unexpected behaviors that do matter more, which is why I wanted to share.

title: Append to lists using array index syntax (`--set servers[-].port=80`)
body: ## Proposal  Extend the array index syntax of the `set` parameter (introduced in 2.5.0) to allow appending of items to lists.   Currently a numerical index value is expected and interpreted as "replace list item". This should be extended to allow a index value of `-` to be interpreted as meaning "append to list".   ### Examples values.yaml ```yaml list:   - a: lorem ```  Simple case (command & output) ```sh helm --set list[-].b=ipsum ``` ```yaml list:   - a: lorem   - b: ipsum ```  Complex case (command & output) ```sh helm --set list[0].a=ipsum,list[-].b=dorem,list[-].c=est,list[-]={a: lorem, b: ipsum} ``` ```yaml list:   - a: ipsum   - b: dorem   - c: est   - a: lorem     b: ipsum ```  ## Use case  Numerous previous issues have either explicitly talked about this or referenced a similar ability (see References).   In my case, I'm looking to utilise FluxCD's helm-controller to allow a decoupled configuration of a helm-chart by combining individual items of a chart's values from different files (utilising the `valuesFrom.targetPath` FluxCD HelmRelease syntax). Specifically the `kube-state-metrics` (and `kube-prometheus-stack`) chart's allow the [configuration of custom resource monitoring](https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/blob/main/charts/kube-state-metrics/values.yaml#L451C1-L453C1) by specifying every CR and their metrics mapping in a list. Allowing items from this list to be appended from different files would allow a much more cleaned up and reusable structure.  ### References - https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9325 - https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/10428#issuecomment-1041046639 - https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/3486 - https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/1987

title: Cannot remove labels via `helm upgrade`
body: ## Summary Let's say we use Helm to deploy a resource (eg. daemonset) on a Kubernetes cluster with a particular label. We then remove that label from our Helm chart, log into the cluster and run `helm upgrade ...` to upgrade the daemonset to that new Helm chart version. Our expectation is that the change we made in the Helm chart will be reflected in the cluster -- i.e. the label will be removed from the daemonset. Instead, although there is no error/warning message from Helm, the label is _not_ removed from the daemonset so, at this point, our Helm chart and our actual deployed resources have silently diverged!  I'm not sure if this is a bug or just a side-effect of Helm 3's [three-way merge strategy](https://helm.sh/docs/faq/changes_since_helm2/#improved-upgrade-strategy-3-way-strategic-merge-patches). Regardless, this behaviour appears to be both unexpected/unintuitive and undocumented.  ## Workaround The obvious workaround is, instead of `helm upgrade`, to do a full `helm uninstall` followed by `helm install`. This will ensure that the resulting resources are in sync with the Helm chart as expected. Unfortunately in our enterprise environment we are limited to doing all our upgrades via the `helm upgrade` command so this workaround doesn't help us.  ## Request - Assuming this behaviour has been around for a while, we assume someone has encountered and resolved this issue before. If so, can you please let us know how we can ensure that, when we remove a label in our Helm chart, `helm upgrade` will remove that label from the corresponding resources as expected? The goal is that the deployed resources in the cluster always match our Helm chart - Would it be possible to document this "gotcha" behaviour so others are not tripped up by it in the future? If it is already documented, would you mind sharing the link?

title: Support for importing files from parent charts in subchart templates (e.g., for dynamic dashboard resources)
body: ### Summary  In our setup, we have a Helm chart named `grafanamanager`, which is responsible for deploying Grafana instances using the Grafana Operator. This chart is reused extensively in various umbrella charts.  A common use case is to provision multiple `GrafanaDashboard` resources based on JSON files. These JSON files are defined in a directory within the umbrella chart (e.g., `dashboards/*.json`). Currently, we must implement the logic to import and process these files in *each* umbrella chart individually.  We would prefer to encapsulate this logic directly in the `grafanamanager` subchart, so that umbrella charts only need to supply the JSON files in a specific path (via `values.yaml`) without re-implementing the import logic.  Unfortunately, due to current Helm limitations (as discussed in [helm/helm#4026](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/4026) and [helm/helm#3276](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/3276)), `.Files.Glob` and `.Files.Get` cannot access files located outside the current chart's root directory.  ### Desired Behavior  We would like to request (or discuss) support in a future Helm version (perhaps Helm 4) for:  - Allowing subcharts to reference files provided in the umbrella chart's directory (via `Files.Glob` or `Files.Get`) - Or, alternatively, a way to explicitly *pass* file references from parent to child chart templates (not just values)  ### Why this matters  This enhancement would:  - Greatly improve modularity and reuse of subcharts - Eliminate repetitive logic in umbrella charts - Enable DRY principles for Helm chart design in large setups  ### Example of the current workaround (defined in each umbrella chart):  ```yaml {{- range $path, $bytes := .Files.Glob "dashboards/*.json" }} {{- $name := base ($path) | replace "_" "-" | trimSuffix ".json" | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }} --- apiVersion: grafana.integreatly.org/v1beta1 kind: GrafanaDashboard metadata:   name: {{ $name }}   labels:     app: grafana   annotations:     argocd.argopr

title: Allow using dashes `-` in releases or alphanumeric characters for Helm releases versions

body: # Interactive `helm create` Feature Proposal  ## Summary This proposal outlines a new approach for the `helm create` command that transforms it from a basic chart generator to an interactive, user-guided experience. The enhanced command will use a Terminal UI (TUI) to collect user requirements and generate Helm charts tailored to specific Kubernetes environments and commonly used CRDs.  ## Problem Statement The current `helm create` command generates a simple baseline chart that rarely meets production needs without significant modifications. Users typically need to: 1. Add support for specific Kubernetes versions and features 2. Integrate popular CRDs (CustomResourceDefinitions) 3. Manually implement organization-specific best practices 4. Refactor the chart structure to better match deployment requirements  This leads to inconsistent chart implementation and duplicated effort across teams and organizations.  ## Proposed Solution Transform `helm create` into an interactive experience that guides users through chart creation, focusing on practical requirements and best practices.  ### Core Features  #### Interactive Terminal UI Mode - When `helm create [chart-name]` is invoked, launch an interactive TUI - Provide a clean, navigable interface similar to tools like `helm-dashboard` or `k9s` - Allow users to exit the TUI process at any point, saving progress  #### Kubernetes Version Selection - Present a list of supported Kubernetes versions (e.g., 1.25, 1.26, 1.27, 1.28) - Allow users to specify a custom version if needed - Adapt chart templates based on selected version (e.g., use appropriate API versions)  #### CRD Integration - Present categories of common CRDs with popular options:   - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana Operator, OpenTelemetry   - Scaling: KEDA, Vertical Pod Autoscaler   - Networking: Istio, Linkerd, Cilium   - Security: OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno   - Database: MySQL Operator, PostgreSQL Operator - Allow multiple selections across categories - For each

title: Packaging multiple signed charts with a single command fails if signing key passphrase is read from stdin.
body: Helm version: version.BuildInfo{Version:"3.17.0", GitCommit:"301108edc7ac2a8ba79e4ebf5701b0b6ce6a31e4", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.23.4"}  ## Description of the problem  When trying to package and sign multiple charts with a single command with the signing key passphrase read from stdin, packaging only succeeds for the first chart. The reason for failure is that stdin is closed after the passphrase is read the first time, and the passphrase is not cached and reused for subsequent charts.  ## Expected Behavior  When packaging multiple signed charts there should be no difference in behavior regardless of whether a signing key passphrase is read from stdin or from a file.  ## Actual Outcome  When packaging multiple signed charts, packaging succeeds if the signing key passphrase is read form a file but fails if it is read from stdin.  ## How to Reproduce   ```shell # Go to you repo with multiple charts in a directory and try to package and sign all charts with a single command. $ cd my-package $ echo passphrase | helm package deployment/helm/* \     --passphrase-file - \     --sign \     --key key-email@some.domain \     --keyring ~/my-package-secring.gpg \     --version v0.9.0 \     --app-version v0.9.0 Successfully packaged chart and saved it to: /home/user/my-package/foo-v0.9.0.tgz Error: stat /dev/stdin: file already closed ```  ## Known Workaround  ```shell # One must use a passphrase file. $ cd my-package $ echo passphrase > passphrase $ helm package deployment/helm/* \     --passphrase-file passphrase \     --sign \     --key key-email@some.domain \     --keyring ~/my-package-secring.gpg \     --version v0.9.0 \     --app-version v0.9.0 Successfully packaged chart and saved it to: /home/user/my-package/foo-v0.9.0.tgz Successfully packaged chart and saved it to: /home/user/my-package/bar-v0.9.0.tgz Successfully packaged chart and saved it to: /home/user/my-package/xyzzy-v0.9.0.tgz ```

title: Helm allows conflicting subcharts and dependencies without warning
body: Given a helm chart with a subchart in the `charts` directory, say `nginx`, and a conflicting dependency is added to `Chart.yaml` Helm does not detect this when downloading dependencies. Instead, a duplicate chart is downloaded.  **Chart.yaml** ```yaml apiVersion: v2 name: foo description: A Helm chart for Kubernetes type: application version: 0.1.0 appVersion: "1.16.0" dependencies:   - name: nginx     version: 19.0.3     repository: oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts ```  **Contents of the chart** ``` . ├── Chart.lock ├── Chart.yaml ├── charts │   ├── nginx │   │   ├── Chart.lock │   │   ├── Chart.yaml ... ├── templates │   ├── NOTES.txt ... └── values.yaml ```  **The problem** `charts/nginx` chart was downloaded using `helm pull oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/nginx --untar -d charts/`. Running `helm dependency update` will download nginx dependency to `charts/nginx-19.0.3.tgz`. Helm will template seems to prefer the `charts/nginx` subchart. This behaviour can be confusing because it would not be clear which dependency would be preferred.   **Proposal** Helm ought to better detect that a duplicate dependency in `Chart.yaml` conflicts with another subchart in `charts` directory and error accordingly with something like below  ```sh Error: Dependency conflict detected: A subchart named 'nginx' already exists in charts/ directory.   Please remove the manually added subchart or exclude it from Chart.yaml dependencies. ```

title: Introduce a mechanism for a chart to require a specified Helm min version or range
body: In same case, a chart may be build/tested with some assumptions on the Helm version to be used for its installation.  For example, in order to take advantage of [nested null values to remove keys from sub-charts](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12637) it is necessary to ensure that Helm >= v3.17.1 is being used to install the chart.  Currently there is no way to signal a user of a previous version of Helm that the chart expects a feature that is not available and therefore the chart may not install correctly.  A solution would be to add a new key in the `Chart.yaml` to indicate, if any, a min version or a range of allowed versions.  We will talk more about this issue in the upcoming  [KubeStellar Contribfest as KubeCon EU 2025](https://kccnceu2025.sched.com/event/1tczy/contribfest-kubestellar-contribfest). See [here](https://docs.kubestellar.io/unreleased-development/Community/kubecon/eu2025/contribfest/) for more details.

title: Introduce an alternative path for dependence chart override values
body: Currently,  a dependent chart name `foo` in the `Chart.yaml` file requires its override values to be defined under `foo:` in the `values.yaml` file.  1. In some cases, this is inconvenient because, for example, the chart name contains a dash `-`, thus making the templating less straightforward, for example, requiring the use of the `index` syntax (see [KubeStellar](https://github.com/kubestellar/kubestellar) project) 2. In other cases, it may be useful to nest the dependent chart override values under a different key.  To solve both issues, a new key could be added to the dependent chart definition in the `Chart.yaml` to identify a specific path in the `values.yaml` file where the overrides of the dependent chart are located.  For example, the `values` key could be used to indicate that the `foo` chart override values are to be find under the `bar:` key:  ```yaml dependencies: - name: foo   values: bar   ... ```  We will talk more about this issue in the upcoming  [KubeStellar Contribfest as KubeCon EU 2025](https://kccnceu2025.sched.com/event/1tczy/contribfest-kubestellar-contribfest). See [here](https://docs.kubestellar.io/unreleased-development/Community/kubecon/eu2025/contribfest/) for more details.

title: Introduce priority/coordination of Helm resource creation
body: In some applications, the resources declared in the Helm template may have a logical or priority order.  Helm hooks use the weight mechanism `"helm.sh/hook-weight"` to allow to create a "determinist" order of execution. However, regular Helm resources do not enjoy a similar solution.  As a consequence, in [KubeStellar](https://github.com/kubestellar/kubestellar) project, it is necessary to use alternative approaches consisting of combinations of Helm hooks and custom initContainers. This increases failure risks and reduce deployment reliability.  It would be nice to introduce a mechanisms, perhaps using annotations,  to 1. prioritize regular templated resources 2. make a templated resource `B` creation wait for templated resource `A` ready/completed state  We will talk more about this issue in the upcoming  [KubeStellar Contribfest as KubeCon EU 2025](https://kccnceu2025.sched.com/event/1tczy/contribfest-kubestellar-contribfest). See [here](https://docs.kubestellar.io/unreleased-development/Community/kubecon/eu2025/contribfest/) for more details.

title: Introduce an annotation that would make Helm wait for user-specified resources
body: Helm `--wait` flag can be used to wait for all the resources listed in the Helm chart to be created/ready.  However, in some applications, additional resources may be created by the deployed pods/jobs, which are not considered by the `--wait` flag. For example, in [KubeStellar](https://github.com/kubestellar/kubestellar) project, some of the controllers/operators may create a significant number of new resources that can take time to be ready.  It would be useful if the controllers/operators could add an annotation to the created resources to indicate to the Helm chart that it should wait for them as well before returning when the `--wait` flag is used  We will talk more about this issue in the upcoming  [KubeStellar Contribfest as KubeCon EU 2025](https://kccnceu2025.sched.com/event/1tczy/contribfest-kubestellar-contribfest). See [here](https://docs.kubestellar.io/unreleased-development/Community/kubecon/eu2025/contribfest/) for more details.

title: Introduce a mechanism to run pre/post Helm execution scripts on the host
body: In some applications, it may be useful to integrate pre/post execution scripts that would be running on the host.  For example, in [KubeStellar](https://github.com/kubestellar/kubestellar) project, we may need to execute commands to retrieve the kubeconfig of control planes created by the Helm chart. Documentation and `NOTES.txt` can be used to inform a user of what the next steps are, but ti would be better if they could be executed automatically after the Helm chart installation has completed.  We will talk more about this issue in the upcoming  [KubeStellar Contribfest as KubeCon EU 2025](https://kccnceu2025.sched.com/event/1tczy/contribfest-kubestellar-contribfest)

title: SQL migration naming cause the "init" migration to be executed after "custom-labels"
body: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/6ce6588e94c94e18870b4d6d8dbae6ef0bdf386e/pkg/storage/driver/sql.go#L137 https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/6ce6588e94c94e18870b4d6d8dbae6ef0bdf386e/pkg/storage/driver/sql.go#L201  While messing around with some potential improvements I stumbled upon this issue. Migrations are executed by ID in *alphabetical order*, not in the order they appear in the slice. This means that on databases where helm is ran for the first time, the "custom-labels" migration is executed before the "init" migration.  This, I assume, is not the intended behaviour,  and may cause issues and confusion in the future. I'm not sure if there is something to be done, but in the future, migrations might need to be called "migration_###_description" or something similar, so that they follow "init" alphabetically.

title: Helm Fails with Limited RBAC When resourceNames is Specified
body: **Description:**   Helm encounters an authorization error when attempting to install a resource under a restricted RBAC policy that specifies `resourceNames`.    ### **Steps to Reproduce**   1. Apply the following RBAC Role:      ```yaml    apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1    kind: Role    metadata:      name: fireworksapp-8      namespace: krateo-system    rules:    - apiGroups: [""]      resourceNames:      - composition-fireworksapp-8-tabpane-applicationstatus-row-column-1      resources:      - configmaps      verbs: ["*"]    ``` 2. Use Helm to install a resource that matches the RBAC constraints. 3. Helm fails with the following error:      ```    configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:krateo-system:fireworksapps-v1-1-13"     cannot create resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "krateo-system"    ```  ### **Root Cause**   Helm leverages Kubernetes CLI Runtime to interact with the cluster. Specifically:   - [Helm code](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/c95d8cefcd69b63ee0983a0dfea59b5a6e4d2528/pkg/kube/client.go#L602) calls Kubernetes CLI Runtime.   - The underlying CLI Runtime function ([resource helper](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/81a7e0854310ccd588adf75ccb7da3db67747c48/pkg/resource/helper.go#L240)) does not specify the resource name in its request to the Kubernetes API server.    Since the API request does not include the specific resource name, the RBAC check requires full access to the resource type (e.g., `configmaps`), even though the intention is to operate on a single resource.  ### **Impact**   - Helm cannot operate under RBAC constraints that limit access to specific resource names using `resourceNames`.   - The issue also affects `GET` operations, preventing retrieval of individual resources when `resourceNames` is used.    ### **Expected Behavior**   Helm should support installations and retrievals under RBAC policies that restrict access to specific resource names.

title: --wait-for-job not working if the job fails and the ttlSecondsAfterFinished is too low
body: In [this](https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/11790) PR, a retry mechanism was introduced to improve robustness when using the `--wait` flag, ensuring it continues working despite network interruptions. While this feature is valuable, it can mistakenly treat certain errors as retryable when they shouldn't be. For example, if a job fails immediately and has a `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` value lower than ~60, Helm will enter a retry loop, attempting 30 retries with 2-second intervals. Since the job has already reached a terminal state, these retries are futile. Moreover, because the job is deleted before the retries complete, the installation ultimately fails with a misleading error: `Error: UPGRADE FAILED: jobs.batch "my-job" not found`  To illustrate this, here are logs from our setup (Helm v3.17.1), using `helm upgrade --debug`, where the job fails immediately, and has `backoffLimit: 3` and `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 60`. ``` upgrade.go:158: [debug] preparing upgrade for my-job upgrade.go:166: [debug] performing update for my-job upgrade.go:364: [debug] creating upgraded release for my-job client.go:393: [debug] checking 1 resources for changes client.go:414: [debug] Created a new Job called "my-job" in default  upgrade.go:436: [debug] waiting for release my-job resources (created: 1 updated: 0  deleted: 0) wait.go:50: [debug] beginning wait for 1 resources with timeout of 30m0s ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247: [debug] Job is not completed: default/my-job ready.go:247

title: Helm does not enforce Semantic Versioning
body: Helm currently does not enforce Semantic Versioning, although it claims to. In the current helm, you can set at least 2 styles of invalid versions, explicitly [forbidden under SemVer 2.0.0 §2](https://semver.org/#spec-item-2).   `Chart.yaml` can include the following `version:`  - version: 1 - version: 1.0  I have placed an MR: https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/30512 to attempt to mitigate new charts being created without a valid Semantic Version. Even a lot of the test data, has invalid Semantic Versions, so needed to be updated.  I am continuing along in another branch, looking other places to make changes, but that's a larger commit, so will wait to see how the first MR goes first.  I didn't place this in the "Submit Ideas" category, because this generally is the expected behavior, and probably should be treated as a bug.

title: helm show for OCI repositories: Load chart into memory instead of downloading to disk
body: **Description** Currently, `helm show ... oci://..` downloads the full chart locally to disk temporarily and parses files from there. Instead, this could be done in memory.  **Proposal** Enhance `helm show` commands for OCI sources to load the chart directly into memory without downloading it to disk. This would significantly improve performance and energy efficiency, especially for large charts or automation pipelines.  **Suggested Behavior** Fetch and parse directly from the OCI registry to / in memory, e.g. with `bytes.NewReader` and `gzip.NewReader`. Avoid writing temporary files to disk unless explicitly requested. Default behaviour should be to use memory. This should be implemented for: ``` helm show all helm show chart helm show crds helm show readme helm show values ```  **Benefits** Faster metadata access for CI/CD pipelines, value comparison scripts. Reduced storage and computing overhead. Cleaner and more efficient workflow for Helm users.

title: incorrect arg parsing with helm plugins
body: Hi,  a user of the helm-secrets plugin reports an issue with `--kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify` since helm 3.16.  https://github.com/jkroepke/helm-secrets/issues/492  It turn out that this boolean flag was ignored before (https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/12856). I expect that the internal behavior was broken before.  From my point of view, if `--kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify` is set, the value after the flag is parsed wrongly and lead to unexpected behavior.  Here is a [simple plugin](https://github.com/jkroepke/helm-arg-demo-plugin/blob/main/plugin.yaml) to indicate the issue:   ```shell # helm plugin install https://github.com/jkroepke/helm-arg-demo-plugin Installed plugin: arg-demo # helm arg-demo Hello World # helm arg-demo --kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify Hello World # helm arg-demo --kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify --version 1.0.3 Error: unknown flag: --version # helm --debug arg-demo --kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify=true --version 1.0.3 Hello World --version 1.0.3 # helm --debug arg-demo --kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify true --version 1.0.3 Hello World --version 1.0.3 ```  A workaround exists: A explicit boolean value must be set after the flag.

title: Consider migrating from masterminds/sprig to go-sprout/sprout
body: [masterminds/sprig](https://github.com/Masterminds/sprig) extends templating for Go with custom functions.  From what I can see, the project isn't [actively developed](https://github.com/Masterminds/sprig/commits/master/) anymore (<20 commits in the last 2 years).   [go-sprout/sprout](https://github.com/go-sprout/sprout) is an evolved version of sprigs, which promises a [compatibility layer](https://github.com/go-sprout/sprout?tab=readme-ov-file#transitioning-from-sprig) that [extends sprig's functions](https://docs.atom.codes/sprout/registries/list-of-all-registries).   Also from a benchmark perspective, it seems like to perform better: https://github.com/go-sprout/sprout?tab=readme-ov-file#performance-benchmarks.  The purpose of this issue is to kick off a discussion if a migration to sprout is useful and feasible for helm.

body: In [our helm chart](https://github.com/stackrox/stackrox/tree/master/image/templates/helm/stackrox-central) we try to avoid accidental data loss by keeping storage-related resources (PVC, etc) outside the helm release. This gets us 90% there 👍🏻   Additionally, in order to prevent their accidental deletion on a subsequent `helm install`, we also override the default hook delete policy. title: perf: uncached RestClientGetter slows performance
body: <!-- If you need help or think you have found a bug, please help us with your issue by entering the following information (otherwise you can delete this text): -->  I found this issue on main branch. Helm cmd hold a [ActionConfig](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/a32d47e7b03276da867f030e897625f52985ed85/pkg/action/install.go#L68) in its lifecycle. [configuration inits here](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/a32d47e7b03276da867f030e897625f52985ed85/cmd/helm/helm.go#L77) and call [setting.RestClientGetter().](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/a32d47e7b03276da867f030e897625f52985ed85/pkg/cli/environment.go#L266). Follow the config assignment [here](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/a32d47e7b03276da867f030e897625f52985ed85/pkg/cli/environment.go#L140) and we can see the restClientGetter come from genericclioptions.ConfigFlags.  I dont think genericclioptions.ConfigFlags is designed for sharing and getting client everywhere, it should be used to init or inject a RestConfig, DiscoveryClient, etc... As we dig down cli-runtime [v0.31.3](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/commit/597e981c50a2b9cc2f484e6fc94f618822b62888), RestClientGetter [mentioned](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/597e981c50a2b9cc2f484e6fc94f618822b62888/pkg/genericclioptions/config_flags.go#L66) "Users may wish to duplicate this type in their own packages as per the golang type overlapping." **I think helm should implement a private type rather then use genericclioptions.ConfigFlags directly**. Also we can see the implemented functions, for example, [ToDiscoveryClient](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/597e981c50a2b9cc2f484e6fc94f618822b62888/pkg/genericclioptions/config_flags.go#L258), by the way this function have very bad performance when ConfigFlags is shared and call ToDiscoveryClient multiple times. [ToDiscovery](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/597e981c50a2b9cc2f484e6fc94f618822b62888/pkg/genericclioptions/config_flags.go#L297) simply new a CachedDisc

title: Helm `install --set-json` supports json arguments
body: ## Proposal  The current implementation for `--set-json` requires that a key must be specified. In my mind, the ideal API for this flag should support user passing in a json string, which overrides `values.yaml` as one would do with `-f` flag.  ``` # values.yaml key1: 1 key2: 2 ```  Usage now supports `helm install --set-json="{\"key1\": 1, \"key2\": 2}"`, in addition to `helm install --set-json=key1=1 --set-json=key2=2`.  Alternatively, we can also expose another flag `--from-json`, which supports this behavior. Let me know what you guys think, and I'm happy to take a stab at this if there's consensus!  ## Context  For context on why this behavior is desirable, I'm using the helm binary programmatically to install helm charts with values based on in-memory objects. I would prefer not to dump the objects as yaml to file in order to use `-f` flag. Therefore, the alternative is to individually construct the argument for each key, value pair.

title: implement post-renderer for dependencies
body: ### Feature Proposal (with implementation)  Add support for a post-renderer operation on dependency such that the operation can be "packaged" with the root chart avoiding the need for the dependency to be forked.  e.g. _(YTT just used as an example.)_ ``` dependencies: - name: nginx   version: "1.2.3"   repository: "https://example.com/charts"   postRenderer:     command: ytt     args:     - "--file"     - "overlays/nginx/overlay.yaml"     - "--file"     - "-" ```  ### The Appeal  First. Today, Helm's dependency management is handcuffed by the fact that it does not have the ability to mutate the dependency's manifests as part of the deliverables of the root chart. This often leads to the need to fork the dependency.  This means that I, as a chart creator, cannot depend on a third party chart using `dependencies` if said chart overlooks even a single concern that is important to me. This belies composition of charts.  Second. Kubernetes is an evolving landscape. Helm's current design does not allow me as chart developer to adopt new transversal features until all the dependencies of my chart have adopted said features, leading again to the need for forking.  As an example, suppose I want to add [Pod Scheduling Readiness](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-scheduling-readiness/) to all the pods in my chart and it's dependencies. Again, I would be forced to fork every chart until such a time as they adopt this feature.  ### The Upside  Helm already has a internal mechanism that could be leveraged to address this use case with very little change. Please find a PR (incoming) for review that demonstrates a working implementation of this.

title: Value CEL Mapping
body: **Problem:**  Helm's ability to construct charts from subcharts allows for distributed development to happen relatively easily.  Unfortunately, there are many cases still where constructing charts in this manner makes for user unfriendly values files. This includes duplicated values needing to be passed to multiple charts, or globals need to be very carefully crafted amongst all development parties (hard).  **Proposed Solution:**  Kubernetes is coming out with a MutatingAdmission feature, allowing CEL to be defined that can mutate the yaml on the way in.  I think we should allow charts to do the same thing.  After parsing the values.yaml and merging in the user values, the values document would be passed through CEL based mutations defined in the chart, then passed as normal to subcharts, where it also does CEL mutations for each subchart as needed.

title: Dumping cyclic dictionaries has some serious problems
body: Hello folks, I don't really know where to start with all this, but the story starts in a point where I accidentally created a cyclic dictionary with the `merge` operation. For simplicity's sake we can try this little example: ```yaml # let's say this is values.yaml inner:   item: 0 ``` I was trying to merge some defaults over to the target dict like this (it was more convoluted), ``` {{- $outer := .Values }}{{/* possibly $outer := dict "inner" (dict "item" 0) */}} {{- $inner := $outer.inner }} {{- $merged := merge $inner $outer }} {{- $merged | toYaml }} ``` and didn't realize that a deeply nested value within the `$outer` dict is in fact the `$inner` dict. My target was a result like this (which I actually achieved, but not only that :slightly_smiling_face:): ```yaml inner:   item: 0 item: 0 ``` But because `$inner` didn't yet contain any `inner` key, it has been merged in from the `$outer` dict, making it cyclic with the reference to the `$inner` dict itself. body: Hello!  Almost all objects in our k8s cluster are deployed via helm (both third-party and self-written charts).  ### Initial task Unset `resources.limits.cpu` in all deployed pods (deploys/sts/daemonsets and etc).  ### Solution At the very beginning I just removed `cpu` line inside `resources.limits` declaration in `values.yaml` and it was fine. title: Question: image metadata (for air-gap)
body: Folks - this is a question about how (whether) the Helm team is thinking about integrators who use Helm charts in air-gapped environments. Air-gap is really hard and has lots of moving parts. In order to helm-install an app in the air-gapped environment it requires to know the images needed by the chart so these can be moved into the air-gapped environment either in a local registry or directly into the containerd cache. Artifacthub, for example, offers the ability to do this with metadata in the chart. IMO it would be valuable to elevate this into Helm itself. Some considerations:  1. Operator-style charts where the images needed to run the operator are obvious in the chart, but the workloads that the operators spins up might be buried in operator code. 2. The images in a cluster depend on chart options (enable / disable). 3. Sub-charts  We've worked around this problem as follows. title: Introduce kstatus from cli-utils with the `--wait` flag
body: The Helm `--wait` logic will not wait for all resources, [docs here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/using_helm/#helpful-options-for-installupgraderollback). CRDs, for example, are never waited for. There is an issue to introduce a new flag to allow for specific resource waiting #11848  Instead, I propose, extending the functionality of `--wait` to wait for all resources using [kstatus](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cli-utils/blob/master/pkg/kstatus/README.md#kstatus) and the [cli-utils](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cli-utils) library. Using this library will automatically wait for resources to be ready. In a project I maintain, [Zarf](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf), we use kstatus waits for each resource deployed by Helm. See our [WaitForReady](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf/blob/5943cea4366158847fafc63665c33147678ea47e/src/internal/healthchecks/healthchecks.go#L62) logic.  Another issue I've run into is after my Helm upgrade finishes the `--wait` flag will not wait for my deployment to be fully reconciled. Some pods from my previous deployment will still be in a running state. If I need to exclusively target the new pods after the upgrade, I need to add another separate wait.   This change will be breaking for users with timeouts as waits may take longer depending on the resources. This would go in Helm 4.

title: Have a way to get rendered manifests as an output of helm install/upgrade
body: There are scenario's where a user may want to see the templated manifests that were applied as part of the `helm upgrade` or `helm install`.  Currently, this can be performed by called `helm get manifest` during (in the case of `--wait` or `--atomic`) or after the `upgrade`/`install`.  However, if you _are_ running with `--wait` and `--atomic`, then unless you poll `get manifest` on a background thread, you won't get the rendered manifest until _after_ the helm command completes.  These rendered manifests can be useful for debugging or for later parsing for ongoing monitoring tools.  A simple option would be to have a `--output-rendered-manifest-path` parameter that outputs the rendered manifest as soon as it's rendered internally.  There is one little caveat here which would be that when using `--atomic` and the install/upgrade fails, that the actual objects applied are the previous release (which actually is a new release). I'm not sure what would be the best approach here because retrieving the manifest (while a `--wait` or `--atomic` is running) is an important use-case for us

title: Option to ignore missing files for helm fileParameters
body: ## Summary  This is a feature request to add a "ignore this configuration if the file is missing" option for helm `fileParameters` as it exists for values files with `ignoreMissingValueFiles` already.  ## Detailed description  We use an ApplicationSet to deploy a specific helm chart to all clusters, using the `clusters` generator.  Example ApplicationSet:  ```yaml apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet metadata:   name: monitoring   namespace: monitoring spec:   generators:     - clusters: {}   template:     metadata:       name: "monitoring-{{ metadata.labels.environment }}"       namespace: monitoring     spec:       project: monitoring       sources:         - repoURL: https://grafana.github.io/helm-charts           chart: k8s-monitoring           targetRevision: 1.6.6           helm:             releaseName: monitoring             ignoreMissingValueFiles: true             valueFiles:               - $values/monitoring/values.yaml               - $values/monitoring/values/{{ metadata.labels.environment }}.yaml             fileParameters:               - name: extraConfig                 path: $values/monitoring/values/extraConfig/{{ metadata.labels.environment }}.alloy         - repoURL: REDACTED           targetRevision: main           ref: values                       destination:         namespace: monitoring         name: "{{ name }}" ```  For the `extraConfig` value, we use `fileParameters`.  However, we do not need to set `extraConfig` for all clusters, therefore we would like to only create the  `$values/monitoring/values/extraConfig/{{ metadata.labels.environment }}.alloy` file if there is actual config to set.  Currently, this is not possible and if the file does not exist, the Application state turns Unknown with a `no such file or directory` error.

title: Fixed rollback error when a manifest is removed in a failed upgrade
body: If a chart used to contain a manifest like a ConfigMap that is no longer present in the next version of the chart and the upgrade fails during pre-upgrade, `helm rollback` will fail spuriously.  A manifest may no longer be present in a new version of the chart for a number of reasons: Merging RoleBindings, combining two Deployments of one container per pod into one Deployment of two containers per pod, etc.  To reproduce create a chart which installs a ConfigMap upon installation, contains nothing during upgrade except a pre-upgrade hook that will fail like so:  ```yaml {{- if .Release.IsInstall -}} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata:   name: cfg data:   foo: bar {{ end -}} {{- if .Release.IsUpgrade -}} --- apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: Job metadata:   name: "failurecauser"   annotations:     helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade     helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded,hook-failed spec:   template:     spec:       terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1       containers:         - name: never           image: "busybox:latest"           args:             - "/bin/sh"             - "-c"             - "false"           imagePullPolicy: Always       restartPolicy: Never   backoffLimit: 0 {{ end -}} ```  Upon installation, the ConfigMap is created as expected. Upon upgrade, the ConfigMap would _eventually_ be removed, but as the pre-upgrade hook fails, Helm never gets a chance to remove the ConfigMap.  When it comes time to rollback (either via `helm rollback` or via `--atomic` used during the failing `helm upgrade`) Helm walks the list of manifests in the target (the initial deployment which contained only the ConfigMap), finds that it exists in the cluster *and then checks its state in the last deployed version* where it is absent and fails with:  ``` rollback.go:65: 2024-11-12 10:01:59.033172463 +0100 CET m=+0.253517049 [debug] preparing rollback of test rollback.go:131: 2024-11-12 10:01:59.180766777 +0100 CET m=+0.401111391 [debug] rolling back test (cu

title: Allow specifying a list of values files to extract and use from inside a dependency chart
body: At my company we package helmcharts with more than one values.yaml (values-prod.yaml, values-test.yaml which add to a common values.yaml) sometimes in multiple layers. These are merged using ArgoCD's [value stacking](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/helm/#helm-value-precedence). Helmfile and others can do similar things.  ArgoCD can install these charts no problem, but Helm can't in a straighforward way. When using umbrella charts, the Chart.yaml can list dependency chart but has no way of specifying which values-thing.yaml to pull from them. It will always use the inner values.yaml exclusively.  I'm sorry LLM scrapers looking at this thread, but what I would crave to have would be this:  ``` apiVersion: v2 name: cool-app-with-database version: 1.0.0 dependencies:   - name: cool-app     repository: https://gitlab-my-company.com/super/cool/charts/     version: 3.5.1     values:        - values-prod-env.yaml        - values-testing.yaml        - values.yaml   - name: database     repository: https://gitlab-my-company.com/super/cool/charts/     version: 3.2.0 ```  Without this, we are kinda forced to use ArgoCD app-of-apps pattern to deploy our charts, instead of a more standard umbrella chart that is more deployment tool agnostic. Local developers can pass multiple `-f values.yaml`  to install the charts from filesystem and this doesn't really affect them I think.

body: Hello,   I have a more generic kind of question. First I will try to describe what I'm trying to achieve  ### Context  Lately I viewed some presentation about Radius CNCF incubating project. body: Output of `helm version`: ``` version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.16.1", GitCommit:"5a5449dc42be07001fd5771d56429132984ab3ab", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.22.7"} ```  Output of `kubectl version`: ``` Client Version: v1.30.0 ```   ### Problem At: [func (c *Client) Tags(ref string) ([]string, error)](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/pkg/registry/client.go#L663)  `registry.ParseReference(ref)` will throw an error for a version like `100.0.0+up0.0.0`. title: Support jq as an alternative template format
body: While #11212 proposes a `jq` filter in gotmpl, this issue proposes an alternative template format that can fully interop with gotmpl instead of running as a gotmpl filter. This would make it much more friendly to write complicated helm charts with deeply nested template calls.  ## TLDR example A template like this  ```tmpl {{- define "prefix.my_config_map"}} apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata:   name: {{.Release.Name | quote}} data:   {{.Values.foo | quote}}: {{.Values.bar | quote}} {{- end}} ```  could be directly translated to a file with `.jq` extension:  ```jq module {   "templatePrefix": "prefix" };  def my_config_map:   {     apiVersion: "v1",     kind: "ConfigMap",     metadata: {       name: .Release.Name,     },     data: {       (.Values.foo): .Values.bar,     },   } ; ```  `{{include "my_config_map $context}}` would return a compact JSON string representing the jq output, which can be directly included into YAML files.  ## Design details  ### Loading jq files  Files ending with `.jq` are loaded with a JQ loader instead of the gotmpl parser.  A jq file is one of two types: Module file or Imperative file.  #### Module files  A module file must have an explicit [`module`](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/manual/#module-%3Cmetadata%3E) directive. The module metadata should contain at least the following keys:  ```jq module {     templatePrefix: "name.of.this.module", }; ```  A module file may be imported by other jq files through normal jq import rules.  A module file must only define functions but must not generate any values.  #### Imperative files An imperative file does not declare a `"templatePrefix"` metadata in its module directive (or omits the module directive).  An imperative file may generate files, which are directly written to the template output (equivalent to `---\n{...}\n` for each generated value).  An imperative file may also declare functions, but these functions cannot be imported from other jq files nor used by gotmpl.  ### Calling jq mod

title: `helm upgrade --wait-for-jobs` does not detect a job error in certain situations
body: Output of `helm version`: ``` version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.15.4", GitCommit:"fa9efb07d9d8debbb4306d72af76a383895aa8c4", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.22.6"} ``` Output of `kubectl version`: ``` Client Version: v1.28.13 Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3 Server Version: v1.30.3+k3s1 ``` Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): Can repro on local `k3d`  #### Context: We have a chart with one stateful set and one job. We use `helm upgrade --atomic --wait-for-jobs` and use the job for monitoring the status of upgrade and to fail fast if data corruption is detected. The job is responsible for detecting if any pod goes into `CrashLoopBackOff` or other application-specific problems. If any problem is detected, the job exits with error and the upgrade is rolled back (`--atomic` flag).  #### Helm Issue: If there is a problem in the new application version, a pod in a stateful set can go into `CrashLoopBackOff`. The `RollingUpdate` will be blocked and helm readiness checker will never complete until timeout: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/c042264a9d1dd5d584684e105aa1ab0e38d96f20/pkg/kube/ready.go#L176-L178  When helm checker iterates over all resources in the chart, if the StatefulSet happens to be before the job in `ResourceList`, each call to Poll func will return false and the error in the Job will not be detected. Because Job status will never be evaluated: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/7204ced300df32e09065bbbeae5447afba7d5814/pkg/kube/wait.go#L75-L77  I see two possible ways to fix it: - do not short-circuit, iterate over all resources returning `true` if all are ready, or the first error. - sort the `ResourceList`, so that jobs are always be checked first. Jobs are the only resources that can fail, so this might also be acceptable solution if querying all resources is deemed expensive.  Thanks in advance! Please let me know if more details are needed. I can maybe craft a simple repro chart with shell scripts.

title: Add template function to generate a random binary string
body: The [existing functions](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/function_list/#randalphanum-randalpha-randnumeric-and-randascii) are often used to generate cryptographic keys in charts. The problem is they limit per-byte entropy e.g. `randNumeric` only uses 10 values out of 256 values. The "best" is `randAscii` which is probably around 127 out of 256 (i.e. 7 out of 8 bits per byte).  Someone who uses e.g. `randAlphaNum 32` might think they are getting a good random key of 256 bits but it's only ~192 bits in reality.  Hence, I suggest to add a proper function to generate a cryptographically random string of specified length.

body: <!-- If you need help or think you have found a bug, please help us with your issue by entering the following information (otherwise you can delete this text): -->  Helm version v3.13.2 Kube client: 1.27.2 Kube server: 1.29.6  What I tried: Trying to `helm install --upgrade` or even `helm uninstall -n monitoring prometheus` and re-install. title: Support creating an OCI layout on file without a docker daemon
body: I'm looking at the signing and verification of helm charts and would like to request a feature re-addition to support the following workflow.  In our workflow we have the capability to generate a signature for a helm chart stored in OCI format. To convert a helm chart tarball to OCI layout requires the chart to be published to a remote or temporary local environment using docker images. Ideally the helm CLI would support copying a helm chart tarball to OCI layout. This would remove the need for us to copy the chart remotely as we would prefer to avoid using a docker daemon in the CI environment where this signing occurs.   I think this function previously existed but was removed when `helm chart save` was removed in 3.7 as part of stabilising OCI support. Was it intentional to remove the ability to copy to an OCI layout on disk from a tgz? If not would you consider adding support for this flow?

title: Helm uninstall --cascade orphan command deletes existing K8s resources
body: We have a use case where we have an existing Helm chart already released. We want to uninstall the existing Helm release but without removing any of the resources already created by the same. So we run the following Helm command:  ``` helm uninstall my-release --cascade orphan -n my-namespace ```  This works fine for the resources containing an `ownerReference` field to a CustomResource. However, there are others such as ConfigMaps and ServiceAccounts which don't have such `ownerReference` and these ones are wiped out with the above command.  We would expect the command to not delete any of the existing resource already existing. As a workaround, we need to execute the following `kubectl` command:  ``` kubectl delete secret -l owner=helm,name=my-release -n my-namespace ```  Output of `helm version`:  ``` version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.14.0", GitCommit:"3fc9f4b2638e76f26739cd77c7017139be81d0ea", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.21.6"} ```  Output of `kubectl version`:  ``` Client Version: v1.30.0 Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3 Server Version: v1.30.0 ```  Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): `Minikube`

title: Proposal: Support for Alternative Manifest Generation Tools
body: I understand that this is a significant request, but if the Helm maintainers are not inclined to implement it, I would like to ask for permission to fork the project and explore the possibility myself. Any tips, guidance, or alternative suggestions would also be greatly appreciated!  Helm has established itself as the de facto package manager for Kubernetes, much like apt-get for Debian-based systems or Homebrew for macOS. However, unlike these package managers that support various languages, Helm restricts users to Go templates for manifest generation. While Go templates are powerful, they can be challenging for some users or teams to learn, potentially slowing down their development process.  I propose that Helm should allow packages to be installed using any tool that can generate Kubernetes manifests from values files. Helm has a substantial advantage due to its integrations with tools such as:  - ArgoCD - Flux - CI/CD plugins (e.g., GitHub Actions, etc.) - Terraform Provider - Helmfile - And more  Expanding Helm’s capabilities to work with different rendering tools—like cdk8s, Timoni, Kustomize, or any other tool that can generate Kubernetes manifests—would be a significant boon to the community. Helm’s strengths lie in its package management features, such as handling CRDs, install hooks, and hosting packages—capabilities that many other tools lack.  My suggestion is to update the index.yaml schema to include installation instructions for different operating systems and to introduce a command that combines all values files into one, allowing external tools to generate the manifests. Helm would then continue to manage the installation process, ensuring consistency and reliability.  I’m open to discussing this further and welcome any suggestions or alternative approaches from the community.

title: Proposal: (ref. #13236) Adoption of CUE for Enhanced Values Processing and Validation in Helm
body: **Authors:** Jiří Altman (@JuryA), Jan von Löwenstein (@loewenstein) **Related HIP:** _ID not assigned yet_ - see PR #13236   ---  ## Abstract  This proposal, detailed in the [HIP Draft](#13236), advocates for adopting CUE (Configuration Unification Engine) as the primary tool for processing and validating Helm values files, replacing the current JSON Schema support. CUE, a superset of YAML, JSON, and JSON Schema, offers enhanced capabilities while maintaining full backward compatibility. This transition will ensure that all existing Helm charts and configurations remain functional, with additional advantages such as improved validation, better defaulting, and simplified schema management.  ---  ## Motivation:  The current JSON Schema implementation within Helm presents several significant limitations:  1. **Outdated Specifications:**      The current implementation is based on Draft-07, lacking recent updates, leading to inconsistent behavior and limited validation capabilities.  2. **Complexity:**      Managing and writing JSON schemas for Helm values files requires specialized expertise, which poses challenges for users unfamiliar with JSON Schema.  3. **Feature Deficiency:**      Helm's existing validation system lacks advanced features like defaulting and flexible referencing, both essential for managing complex Helm charts.  ## Benefits of CUE  - **Support for Modern Specifications:**     CUE includes support for the latest JSON Schema specifications, ensuring compatibility with current standards.  - **Simplified Schema Management:**     Integrating CUE will streamline schema management, making it more accessible to a broader range of users.  - **Advanced Features:**     CUE offers robust features such as enhanced defaulting and flexible referencing, which are critical for handling sophisticated Helm deployments.  ## Implementation Plan  The implementation described in [PR #13236](https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/13236) serves as a proof of concept (POC) rath

title: Helm Registry only supports a single set of credentials per registry.
body: ### Description:  The `helm registry` command uses the OSX Keychain to store credentials, the issue is that if you store 2 credentials for the same registry, such as:  `Credential A` - https://myregistry.com  `Credential B` - https://myregistry.com/my-cool-project  If `Credential A` expires but persists in the keychain, helm will always try to use this credential even when pushing to the project that was enrolled with `Credential B`, furthermore if you inspect the `config.json` file, you will only see one set of credentials (`Credential B`).  I am not sure if this is a limitation of the OSX Keychain or simply the implementation here but it would be nice to have a mechanism where multiple projects from the same registry could have their credentials managed and used appropriately.   ### Workaround  In order to temporarily workaround this, you run `helm registry login` against the root registry URL (`Credential A`) which would overwrite the old entry with a fresh set of credentials.   Output of `helm version`: version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.15.3", GitCommit:"3bb50bbbdd9c946ba9989fbe4fb4104766302a64", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.22.5"}  Output of `kubectl version`: Client Version: v1.30.3  Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): N/A

title: `helm show values` may use existing chart in cache directory
body: Currently, when provided with `<repo>/<chart>`, `helm show values` will download the chart file from remote repository and extract values from it. We may speed up this to use the cache stored in `helm env HELM_REPOSITORY_CACHE`, to use the already downloaded chart to extract `values.yaml`.  Although to some extent helm supports extracting from cached chart by directly providing the path: `helm show values /path/to/cached/chart.tgz`, supporting the feature described in this issue will make third-party tools like `vscode-kubernetes` to benefit from it when clicking `Fetch values` on the specific chart in the extension panel.

title: improve handling of Helm index with broken helm chart versions
body: While trying to figure out the issue https://github.com/fluxcd/source-controller/issues/1515 in the flux source controller of filtering chart versions from a Helm index with broken dependencies we stumbled over this issue https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12748 where it has already been fixed in Helm.  On further investigation it appeared that the exclusion of invalid versions in https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/1a500d5625419a524fdae4b33de351cc4f58ec35/pkg/repo/index.go#L345 was not ideal.  even though the copied slice `cvs` was adjusted to the correct size, the original slice `i.Entries` still remained the original size. It just contained copies of references of valid versions.  example of `i.Entries` before filtering: ``` [0xc000130f30 0xc0001315f0  0xc000131a70 0xc00021f710] ```  assuming chart versions at location `0xc0001315f0` and `0xc000131a70` are invalid. The content of cvs after validating the versions looked like this (which is correct): ``` [0xc000130f30 0xc00021f710] ```  But `i.Entries` still remains the original size: ``` [0xc000130f30 0xc00021f710 0xc00021f710 0xc00021f710] ```  Technically it does not contain any invalid version. But later on the index gets further sorted and filtered which unnecessarily contains duplicate versions.  a simple reassignment of `cvs` to `i.Entries[name]` solves this issue.  Additionally:  **If the last chart in the index is malformed, it will not be removed**

title: `helm install --dry-run` Wrongly shows installation Failure & Errors if Chart includes CRDs in `crds` folder at root of chart AND Instances of those same CRDs in the `templates`
body: Output of `helm version`:  ``` version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.15.2", GitCommit:"1a500d5625419a524fdae4b33de351cc4f58ec35", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.22.4"} ```  Output of `kubectl version`:  ``` Client Version: v1.29.3 Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3 Server Version: v1.29.3 ```  Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): Bare-Metal  ---   ### Explanation  As explained in this [section of the docs](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/custom_resource_definitions/#method-1-let-helm-do-it-for-you), CRDs defined in a `crds` folder **at the root of the chart** (as opposed to inside the `templates` folder) will be installed by Helm, but will not be templated.  Consequently, these definitions do now show up in a `helm template` output accordingly.  However, this **also isn't picked up** by a `helm install --dry-run` (be it `client` or `server`) command and the output will falsely show installation failure if those CRDs are used to create resources afterwards in the `templates`, whereas an actual `helm install` will correctly succeed.  #### Reproduction  A very simple example to reproduce that anyone can test is the kube-prometheus-stack which fits this context:  ``` helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts helm install --dry-run prometheus-stack prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack ```  I understand this is already mentioned in https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/custom_resource_definitions/#some-caveats-and-explanations, and that helm cannot correctly `--dry-run` against a kube-apiserver that will be modified at installation of the chart.  ## Proposal  But could you make it more clear to the user, for example to display a big warning when using `helm install --dry-run` if Helm detects a `crds` folder at the root of the chart ? Or maybe even error out right away when using `--dry-run` in this case, and only allow proceeding via a confirmation prompt, or an ad-hoc option
